title.zh: 卷六十五 志第四十一 輿服一
title.raw: 卷六十五 志第四十一 輿服一 Volume 65 Treatises 41: Carriages and Clothing 1

sentences.zh: 大輅 玉輅 大馬輦 小馬輦 步輦 大涼步輦 板轎 耕根車 后妃車輿 皇太子親王以下車輿 公卿以下車輿 傘蓋 鞍轡

translations.literal: Great State Carriage, Jade Carriage, Large Horse Sedan, Small Horse Sedan, Hand Sedan, Large Cool Hand Sedan, Board Palanquin, Plough-Root Carriage, Empress Consort Carriages, Crown Prince and Princes and Below Carriages, Dukes and Ministers and Below Carriages, Parasols and Canopies, Saddles and Bridles
translations.idiomatic: Great State Carriage; Jade Carriage; large and small horse sedans; hand sedans; large cool hand sedan; board palanquin; plough-root carriage; carriages for empresses and consorts; carriages for the crown prince, princes, and those below; carriages for dukes, ministers, and those below; parasols and canopies; saddles and bridles

sentences.zh: 有虞氏御天下，車服以庸。

translations.literal: When the House of Yu ruled All-under-Heaven, carriages and dress were regulated by merit.
translations.idiomatic: When the House of Yu held the realm, carriage and apparel were assigned according to merit and rank.

sentences.zh: 夏則黻冕致美。

translations.literal: In Xia, patterned caps and robes reached their utmost refinement.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Xia, embroidered caps and ceremonial dress were carried to their finest point.

sentences.zh: 商則大輅示儉。

translations.literal: In Shang, the Great Carriage displayed frugality.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Shang, the Great Carriage was made to exemplify restraint.

sentences.zh: 成周有巾車、典 輅、弁師、司服之職，天子以之表式萬邦，而服車五乘，下逮臣民。

translations.literal: In the completion of Zhou there were the offices of Cap-Maker of Carriages, Director of Carriages, Cap-Master, and Director of Apparel; the Son of Heaven thereby set the pattern for the myriad states, while five grades of service carriages extended down to ministers and commoners.
translations.idiomatic: In mature Zhou there were officers for carriage caps, state carriages, caps, and court dress; the Son of Heaven used them to display the standard for all lands, with five grades of service carriages reaching down to officials and the people.

sentences.zh: 漢承秦制， 御金根爲乘輿，服袀玄以承大祀。

translations.literal: Han inherited the Qin system, using the Golden Root as the imperial carriage and wearing dark ceremonial dress for the great sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: The Han took over Qin institutions, riding the Golden Root carriage as the imperial conveyance and wearing dark sacrificial robes for the major state rites.

sentences.zh: 東都乃有九斿、雲罕、旒冕、絇屨之儀物， 踵事增華，日新代異。

translations.literal: The Eastern Capital then had ritual objects such as the nine tassels, cloud canopy, tasseled crown, and knotted shoes, each generation piling ornament upon ornament, renewing and altering them day by day.
translations.idiomatic: At the Eastern Capital there appeared regalia such as the nine-tasseled banners, cloud canopy, jeweled crown, and knotted court shoes, with each reign adding further splendor until the forms changed from age to age.

sentences.zh: 江左偏安，玉輅棲寶鳳，採旄銜金龍。

translations.literal: The south of the Yangzi held only a partial realm; the jade carriage bore jeweled phoenixes, and colored pennants held golden dragons in their mouths.
translations.idiomatic: In the partial regime south of the Yangzi, jade carriages carried jeweled phoenixes, and colored streamers were fitted with golden dragons.

sentences.zh: 其服冕也，或飾翡 翠、珊瑚、雜珠。

translations.literal: Their ceremonial crowns were sometimes adorned with jadeite, coral, and assorted pearls.
translations.idiomatic: Their ceremonial crowns were sometimes set with jadeite, coral, and mixed pearls.

sentences.zh: 豈古所謂法駕、法服者哉？

translations.literal: How could these be what antiquity called the statutory carriage and statutory dress?
translations.idiomatic: Could these still be what the ancients meant by the prescribed imperial carriage and prescribed court dress?

sentences.zh: 唐武德間著車輿、衣服之制，上得 兼下，下不得擬上。

translations.literal: In the Wude era of Tang, regulations for carriages and clothing were promulgated: those above might encompass those below, but those below might not imitate those above.
translations.idiomatic: During Tang Wude, statutes for carriages and dress were issued: higher ranks could include lower forms, but lower ranks could not adopt higher ones.

sentences.zh: 宋初，袞冕不綴珠玉。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Song, the dragon robe and crown were not strung with pearls and jade.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Song, the dragon robe and crown bore no strings of pearls and jade.

sentences.zh: 政和中詔修車輅，並建旂常，議禮局 所釐定，用爲成憲。

translations.literal: In the Zhenghe era an edict ordered the repair of state carriages and the establishment of banner regalia; what the Bureau for Deliberation on Rites determined was taken as settled statute.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhenghe reign an edict called for restoring the state carriages and setting up the banner regalia; the Ritual Deliberation Bureau fixed the forms, and these became permanent law.

sentences.zh: 元制，郊祀則駕玉輅，服袞冕；

translations.literal: Under Yuan institutions, for suburban sacrifice one rode the jade carriage and wore the dragon robe and crown;
translations.idiomatic: Under Yuan practice, at suburban sacrifice the emperor rode the jade carriage and wore the dragon robe and crown;

sentences.zh: 巡幸，或乘象轎，四時質孫 之服，各隨其宜。

translations.literal: on tours of inspection one sometimes rode an elephant palanquin, and the plain and colored garments of the four seasons were each worn as appropriate.
translations.idiomatic: on imperial tours one sometimes used an elephant palanquin, while the plain and colored seasonal garments were worn as each occasion required.

sentences.zh: 明太祖甫有天下，考定邦禮，車服尚質。

translations.literal: When the Ming Founder had just gained All-under-Heaven, he examined and fixed the state rites, and carriages and dress valued simplicity.
translations.idiomatic: As soon as the Ming Founder secured the realm, he reviewed and fixed the state rituals, keeping carriages and dress plain.

sentences.zh: 酌古通今，合乎禮意。

translations.literal: Weighing antiquity and connecting with the present, they accorded with ritual intent.
translations.idiomatic: Drawing on antiquity while suiting the present, they conformed to ritual propriety.

sentences.zh: 迄於世宗，耤田造耕根，燕居服燕弁，講武用武弁，更爲忠靖冠以風有位，爲保 和冠以親宗藩，亦一王之制也。

translations.literal: Down to the Shizong Emperor, ploughing fields produced the Plough-Root carriage; at ease in the palace one wore the casual cap; for martial instruction one used the military cap; further there were made the Zhongjing cap to admonish those in office and the Baohe cap to draw near imperial clans and feudatories—also the institutions of a single royal house.
translations.idiomatic: By the Shizong reign, the ploughing-field rite produced the Plough-Root carriage; informal residence called for the casual court cap and military drills for the martial cap; the Zhongjing cap was introduced to guide officials in office and the Baohe cap to draw the imperial clan and feudatories near—institutions proper to one dynasty as well.

sentences.zh: 若夫前代傘扇、鞍勒之儀，門戟、旌節之屬，鹹 別等威，至宋加密。

translations.literal: As for the rites of former ages concerning parasols, fans, saddles, and bridles, gate-halberds, banners, and tally-staves, all distinguished grades of majesty, and by the Song these were drawn ever tighter.
translations.idiomatic: As for earlier protocols for parasols, fans, saddles, and bridles, gate halberds, banners, and tally staffs, each rank had its own display of authority, and the Song tightened these distinctions further.

sentences.zh: 明初儉德開基，宮殿落成，不用文石甃地。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Ming, frugal virtue founded the dynasty; when palaces were completed, patterned stone was not used to pave the floors.
translations.idiomatic: Early Ming was founded on frugal virtue: when the palaces were finished, no figured stone was laid for paving.

sentences.zh: 以此坊民，武臣 猶有飾金龍於牀幔，馬廄用九五間數，而豪民亦或熔金爲酒器，飾以玉珠。

translations.literal: By this to restrain the people, yet military officers still ornamented bed curtains with golden dragons, stables used the nine-five bay count, and powerful families also sometimes melted gold into wine vessels and adorned them with jade beads.
translations.idiomatic: Even with this restraint on the people, military officers still put golden dragons on bed curtains, stables were built with the nine-by-five bay pattern, and wealthy families sometimes cast gold wine vessels set with jade beads.

sentences.zh: 太祖 皆重懲其弊。

translations.literal: The Founder in every case severely punished these abuses.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder punished every such abuse severely.

sentences.zh: 乃命儒臣稽古講禮，定官民服舍器用制度。

translations.literal: He then ordered Confucian officials to examine antiquity and expound ritual, fixing the institutions for dress, dwellings, and utensils of officials and commoners.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered scholar-officials to study antiquity and expound ritual, establishing regulations for the dress, housing, and utensils of officials and commoners.

sentences.zh: 歷代守之，遞有禁例。

translations.literal: Each generation preserved them, and in succession there were prohibitory precedents.
translations.idiomatic: Each reign upheld them, and prohibitions accumulated over time.

sentences.zh: 茲更以朝家冊寶、中外符信及宮室器用之等差，附敘於後焉。

translations.literal: Here further, with the gradations of court seals and treasures, internal and external tallies and credentials, and palace furnishings and utensils, these are appended and narrated afterward.
translations.idiomatic: What follows also records the gradations of court seals and treasures, domestic and foreign credentials, and palace furnishings and utensils.

sentences.zh: 天子車輅：明初大朝會，則拱衛司設五輅於奉天門，玉居中，左金，次革， 右象，次木。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven's state carriages: at the beginning of Ming, at great court assemblies the Imperial Guard Office set out the five carriages before the Gate of Receiving Heaven—jade in the center, to the left gold, next leather, to the right ivory, next wood.
translations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven's state carriages: in early Ming, at great court assemblies the Imperial Guard Office arrayed the five carriages before the Gate of Receiving Heaven, with the jade carriage in the center, gold to the left, then leather, ivory to the right, then wood.

sentences.zh: 駕出則乘玉輅，後有腰輿，以八人載之。

translations.literal: When the imperial procession set out he rode the jade carriage; behind was a waist sedan borne by eight men.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor went forth he rode the jade carriage, with a waist sedan carried by eight bearers behind.

sentences.zh: 其後太祖考《周禮》五輅， 以詢儒臣，曰：「玉輅太侈，何若祗用木輅？

translations.literal: Afterward the Founder examined the five carriages in the 《Rites of Zhou》 and questioned the Confucian officials, saying, "The jade carriage is too extravagant—how about using only the wooden carriage?
translations.idiomatic: Later the Founder studied the five carriages in the 《Rites of Zhou》 and asked the scholar-officials, "The jade carriage is too lavish—why not use only the wooden carriage?

sentences.zh: 」博士詹同對曰：「孔子云『乘殷 之輅』，即木輅也。

translations.literal: " Academician Zhan Tong replied, "Confucius said 'ride the carriage of Yin'—that is the wooden carriage.
translations.idiomatic: " Academician Zhan Tong answered, "Confucius said 'ride the carriage of Yin'—that means the wooden carriage.

sentences.zh: 」太祖曰：「以玉飾車，古惟祀天用之，常乘宜用殷輅。

translations.literal: " The Founder said, "To ornament a carriage with jade—in antiquity this was used only for sacrificing to Heaven; for ordinary riding one should use the Yin carriage.
translations.idiomatic: " The Founder said, "Jade ornament on a carriage was used in antiquity only when sacrificing to Heaven; for everyday riding the Yin carriage is appropriate.

sentences.zh: 然 祀天之際，玉輅未備，木輅亦未爲不可。

translations.literal: Yet at the time of sacrificing to Heaven, if the jade carriage is not ready, the wooden carriage is also not impermissible.
translations.idiomatic: Yet if the jade carriage is not ready when sacrificing to Heaven, the wooden carriage is not out of the question.

sentences.zh: 」參政張昶曰：「木輅，戎輅也，不可 以祀天。

translations.literal: " Participating Secretary Zhang Chang said, "The wooden carriage is the military carriage and may not be used to sacrifice to Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: " Participating Secretary Zhang Chang said, "The wooden carriage is the military carriage and cannot be used for sacrifice to Heaven.

sentences.zh: 」太祖曰：「孔子斟酌四代禮樂，以爲萬世法，木輅寧不可祀？

translations.literal: " The Founder said, "Confucius weighed the ritual and music of four dynasties to make the law for ten thousand generations—how could the wooden carriage not be used for sacrifice?
translations.idiomatic: " The Founder said, "Confucius weighed the rites and music of four dynasties to set the model for all time—why should the wooden carriage be unfit for sacrifice?

sentences.zh: 祀在誠 敬，豈泥儀文。

translations.literal: Sacrifice lies in sincerity and reverence—how can one be bound to ceremonial forms?"
translations.idiomatic: Sacrifice rests on sincerity and reverence, not on clinging to ceremonial detail."

sentences.zh: 」洪武元年，有司奏乘輿服御，應以金飾，詔用銅。

translations.literal: " In the first year of Hongwu, the responsible offices memorialized that the imperial carriage and apparel should be ornamented with gold; an edict ordered copper instead.
translations.idiomatic: " In Hongwu 1 the responsible offices proposed gilding the imperial carriage and regalia; the emperor ordered copper instead.

sentences.zh: 有司言費小 不足惜。

translations.literal: The offices said the expense was small and not worth sparing.
translations.idiomatic: The offices said the cost was trifling and not worth worrying over.

sentences.zh: 太祖曰：「朕富有四海，豈吝乎此？

translations.literal: The Founder said, "I possess the four seas in wealth—how could I be stingy about this?
translations.idiomatic: The Founder said, "I possess all within the four seas—would I begrudge this?

sentences.zh: 第儉約非身先無以率下，且奢泰之 習，未有不由小而至大者也。

translations.literal: Only frugality, if the ruler does not take the lead himself, cannot guide those below; moreover the habit of extravagance has never failed to grow from small beginnings to great ones.
translations.idiomatic: But unless the ruler leads in frugality himself, he cannot guide those below; and the habit of extravagance always grows from small things to great.

sentences.zh: 」六年，命禮官考五輅制，爲木輅二乘。

translations.literal: " In the sixth year he ordered ritual officials to examine the institutions of the five carriages and make two wooden carriages.
translations.idiomatic: " In the sixth year he ordered ritual officials to study the five-carriage regulations and commission two wooden carriages.

sentences.zh: 一以丹漆， 祭祀用之；

translations.literal: One was finished in cinnabar lacquer, for use in sacrifice;
translations.idiomatic: One was lacquered cinnabar red for sacrifices;

sentences.zh: 一以皮鞔，行幸用之。

translations.literal: one was covered in leather, for use on imperial tours.
translations.idiomatic: one was leather-covered for imperial tours.

sentences.zh: 是冬，大輅成。

translations.literal: That winter the Great Carriage was completed.
translations.idiomatic: That winter the Great Carriage was finished.

sentences.zh: 命更造大輅一，象輅十，中宮 輅一，後宮車十，飾俱以鳳。

translations.literal: He ordered the further manufacture of one Great Carriage, ten ivory carriages, one central-palace carriage, and ten rear-palace carriages, all ornamented with phoenixes.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered one more Great Carriage, ten ivory carriages, one central-palace carriage, and ten rear-palace carriages, all decorated with phoenixes.

sentences.zh: 以將幸中立府，故造之，非常制也。

translations.literal: Because he was about to visit the Neutral Capital, these were made; they were not the regular institutions.
translations.idiomatic: They were built because he was about to visit the Neutral Capital and were not part of the regular establishment.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，始 定鹵簿大駕之制。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year the institutions of the full guard of honor for the great imperial procession were first fixed.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year the regulations for the full imperial guard of honor were first established.

sentences.zh: 玉輅一，大輅一，九龍車一，步輦一。

translations.literal: One jade carriage, one Great Carriage, one Nine-Dragon Carriage, and one hand sedan.
translations.idiomatic: There were one jade carriage, one Great Carriage, one Nine-Dragon Carriage, and one hand sedan.

sentences.zh: 後罷九龍車。

translations.literal: Later the Nine-Dragon Carriage was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The Nine-Dragon Carriage was later discontinued.

sentences.zh: 永樂三年 更定鹵簿大駕，有大輅、玉輅、大馬輦、小馬輦、步輦、大涼步輦、板轎各一， 具服、幄殿各一。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yongle the full guard of honor for the great procession was revised: there were one each of the Great Carriage, jade carriage, large horse sedan, small horse sedan, hand sedan, large cool hand sedan, and board palanquin, and one each of the full-dress pavilion and canopy hall.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongle 3 the great imperial guard of honor was revised to include one each of the Great Carriage, jade carriage, large and small horse sedans, hand sedan, large cool hand sedan, and board palanquin, plus one full-dress pavilion and one canopy hall.

sentences.zh: 大輅，高一丈三尺九寸五分，廣八尺二寸五分。

translations.literal: The Great Carriage was thirteen feet nine and a half inches in height and eight feet two and a half inches in width.
translations.idiomatic: The Great Carriage stood thirteen feet nine and a half inches high and eight feet two and a half inches wide.

sentences.zh: 輅座高四尺一寸有奇，上平 盤。

translations.literal: The carriage seat was a little over four feet one inch in height, with a level platform above.
translations.idiomatic: The carriage body rose a little over four feet one inch, topped by a level platform.

sentences.zh: 前後車櫺並雁翅及四垂如意滴珠板。

translations.literal: Front and rear carriage rails, together with goose-wing panels and four hanging ruyi pearl-drop boards.
translations.idiomatic: It had front and rear side rails, goose-wing panels, and four hanging ruyi panels with pearl drops.

sentences.zh: 轅長二丈二尺九寸有奇，紅髹。

translations.literal: The shafts were a little over twenty-two feet nine inches long, lacquered red.
translations.idiomatic: The shafts were a little over twenty-two feet nine inches long and lacquered red.

sentences.zh: 鍍金銅 龍頭、龍尾、龍鱗葉片裝釘。

translations.literal: Gilt-bronze dragon heads, dragon tails, and dragon-scale leaf plates were set as fittings.
translations.idiomatic: Gilt-bronze dragon heads, tails, and scale-shaped leaf plates were mounted as fittings.

sentences.zh: 平盤下方箱，四周紅髹，匡俱十二槅。

translations.literal: Below the level platform was a lower box, lacquered red on all four sides, with twelve panels in the frame.
translations.idiomatic: Beneath the platform was a lower box lacquered red on all sides, its frame divided into twelve panels.

sentences.zh: 內飾綠地描 金，繪獸六，麟、狻猊、犀、象、天馬、天祿；

translations.literal: Within it was decorated with green ground and gold tracery, painted with six beasts: qilin, suanni, rhinoceros, elephant, heavenly horse, and heavenly blessing;
translations.idiomatic: Inside it had a green ground with gold tracery, painted with six beasts: qilin, suanni, rhinoceros, elephant, heavenly horse, and tianlu;

sentences.zh: 禽六，鸞、鳳、孔雀、朱雀、翟、 鶴。

translations.literal: six birds: luan, phoenix, peacock, vermilion bird, pheasant, and crane.
translations.idiomatic: and six birds: luan, phoenix, peacock, vermilion bird, pheasant, and crane.

sentences.zh: 盤左右下有護泥板及車輪二，貫軸一。

translations.literal: Below the platform to left and right were mud-guard boards and two wheels, with one axle passing through.
translations.idiomatic: Below the platform on either side were mud guards and two wheels on a single axle.

sentences.zh: 每輪輻十有八，其輞皆紅髹，抹金銅 鈒花葉片裝釘。

translations.literal: Each wheel had eighteen spokes; the rims were all lacquered red, with gilt-bronze inlaid floral leaf plates set as fittings.
translations.idiomatic: Each wheel had eighteen spokes; the rims were lacquered red and fitted with gilt-bronze inlaid floral leaf plates.

sentences.zh: 輪內車心，用抹金銅鈒蓮花瓣輪盤裝釘，軸中纏黃絨駕轅諸索。

translations.literal: Within the wheel at the hub, gilt-bronze inlaid lotus-petal wheel disks were set as fittings; at the center of the axle yellow plush was wound for the shafts and all driving ropes.
translations.idiomatic: At the hub, gilt-bronze lotus-petal disks were inlaid as fittings, and yellow plush was wound around the axle for the shafts and harness ropes.

sentences.zh: 輅亭高六尺七寸九分，四柱長五尺八寸四分。

translations.literal: The carriage pavilion was six feet seven and nine-tenths inches high; the four pillars were five feet eight and four-tenths inches long.
translations.idiomatic: The carriage pavilion stood six feet seven and nine-tenths inches high, with four pillars five feet eight and four-tenths inches long.

sentences.zh: 檻座皆紅髹。

translations.literal: The railing seats were all lacquered red.
translations.idiomatic: The railing bases were all lacquered red.

sentences.zh: 前二柱戧金，柱首寶 相花，中雲龍文，下龜文錦。

translations.literal: The front two pillars were backed with gold; at the pillar heads were treasure-flower motifs, in the middle cloud-dragon patterns, and below tortoise-pattern brocade.
translations.idiomatic: The front two pillars had gold backing; their capitals bore treasure-flower motifs, cloud dragons in the middle, and tortoise-pattern brocade below.

sentences.zh: 前左右有門，高五尺一寸九分，廣二尺四寸九分， 四周裝雕木沉香色描金香草板十二片。

translations.literal: To the front left and right were doors five feet one and nine-tenths inches high and two feet four and nine-tenths inches wide, fitted all around with twelve carved wooden panels in agarwood color with gold tracery of herb patterns.
translations.idiomatic: Doors to the front left and right stood five feet one and nine-tenths inches high and two feet four and nine-tenths inches wide, fitted with twelve carved agarwood-colored panels traced in gold with herb motifs.

sentences.zh: 門旁槅各二及明栨，俱紅髹，以抹金銅 鈒花葉片裝釘，槅編以黃線條。

translations.literal: Beside each door were two panels and open lattices, all lacquered red, set with gilt-bronze inlaid floral leaf plates, the panels woven with yellow cord strips.
translations.idiomatic: Beside each door were two panels and open lattices, all lacquered red and fitted with gilt-bronze floral leaf plates; the panels were woven with yellow cord.

sentences.zh: 後紅髹屏風，上雕描金雲龍五，紅髹板戧金雲龍 一。

translations.literal: At the rear was a red-lacquered screen, carved above with five gold-traced cloud-dragons, and one red-lacquered panel backed with gold cloud-dragons.
translations.idiomatic: At the rear stood a red-lacquered screen carved with five gold-traced cloud dragons above and one red panel backed with gold cloud dragons.

sentences.zh: 屏後地沉香色，上四槅雕描金雲龍四，其次雲板如之。

translations.literal: Behind the screen the ground was agarwood in color; above, four panels carved with four gold-traced cloud-dragons, and below them cloud panels likewise.
translations.idiomatic: Behind the screen the ground was agarwood-colored; above were four panels carved with four gold-traced cloud dragons, with matching cloud panels below.

sentences.zh: 下三槅雕描金雲龍三， 其次雲板亦如之。

translations.literal: Below, three panels carved with three gold-traced cloud-dragons, and below them cloud panels again likewise.
translations.idiomatic: Lower down were three panels with three gold-traced cloud dragons and cloud panels beneath them as well.

sentences.zh: 俱抹金銅鈒花葉片裝釘。

translations.literal: All were set with gilt-bronze inlaid floral leaf plates.
translations.idiomatic: All were fitted with gilt-bronze inlaid floral leaf plates.

sentences.zh: 亭內黃線條編紅髹匡軟座，下蓮花墜 石，上施花毯、紅錦褥席、紅髹坐椅。

translations.literal: Within the pavilion was a soft seat with yellow cord woven in a red-lacquered frame; below was a lotus pendant stone; above were spread a floral carpet, red brocade mattress and mat, and a red-lacquered chair.
translations.idiomatic: Inside the pavilion was a cushioned seat woven with yellow cord in a red-lacquered frame, with a lotus pendant stone below and above it a floral carpet, red brocade bedding, and a red-lacquered chair.

sentences.zh: 靠背上雕描金雲龍一，下雕雲板一，紅髹 福壽板一，並褥。

translations.literal: On the chair back was carved one gold-traced cloud-dragon; below was carved one cloud panel and one red-lacquered fortune-longevity panel, together with cushions.
translations.idiomatic: The chair back bore one carved gold-traced cloud dragon, with a cloud panel below, a red fortune-and-longevity panel, and cushions.

sentences.zh: 椅中黃織金椅靠坐褥，四圍椅裙，施黃綺帷幔。

translations.literal: Within the chair were yellow brocade-with-gold chair-back and seat cushions, a chair skirt on all four sides, and yellow damask curtains hung.
translations.idiomatic: The chair held yellow gold-woven back and seat cushions, a skirt around all four sides, and yellow damask curtains.

sentences.zh: 亭外青綺緣邊 紅簾十扇。

translations.literal: Outside the pavilion were ten red curtains with green damask borders.
translations.idiomatic: Outside the pavilion hung ten red curtains bordered in green damask.

sentences.zh: 輅頂並圓盤，高三尺有奇，鍍金銅蹲龍頂，帶仰覆蓮座，垂攀頂黃線 圓條。

translations.literal: The carriage top and round disk together were a little over three feet high, with a gilt-bronze crouching-dragon finial, bearing upturned and downturned lotus seats, and hanging yellow cord round strips from the climbing top.
translations.idiomatic: The carriage top and round disk together rose a little over three feet, capped by a gilt-bronze crouching dragon with upturned and downturned lotus seats and yellow cord roundels hanging from the finial.

sentences.zh: 盤上以紅髹，其下外四面地沉香色，描金雲；

translations.literal: Above the disk was red lacquer; below it on the outer four sides the ground was agarwood in color with gold-traced clouds;
translations.idiomatic: The disk above was red-lacquered; beneath it on the outer four sides the ground was agarwood-colored with gold-traced clouds;

sentences.zh: 內四角地青，繪五彩云。

translations.literal: within, the four corner grounds were blue, painted with five-colored clouds.
translations.idiomatic: inside, the four corners were blue ground painted with five-colored clouds.

sentences.zh: 以 青飾輅蓋，亭內貼金斗拱，承紅髹匡寶蓋，鬥以八頂，冒以黃綺，謂之黃屋；

translations.literal: The carriage canopy was ornamented in blue; within the pavilion were gilded bracket sets supporting a red-lacquered frame and precious canopy, the bracketing with eight peaks, covered with yellow damask—called the Yellow Canopy;
translations.idiomatic: The carriage canopy was trimmed in blue; inside the pavilion gilded bracket sets supported a red-lacquered precious canopy with eight peaks, covered in yellow damask and called the Yellow Canopy;

sentences.zh: 中 並四周繡五彩雲龍九。

translations.literal: at the center and on all four sides were embroidered nine five-colored cloud-dragons.
translations.idiomatic: at the center and on all four sides were embroidered nine five-colored cloud dragons.

sentences.zh: 天輪三層，皆紅髹，上安雕木貼金邊耀葉板八十一片，內 綠地雕木貼金雲龍文三層，間繪五彩雲襯板八十一片。

translations.literal: The heaven-wheel had three layers, all lacquered red; above were set eighty-one carved wooden gilt-edged radiant leaf plates; within were three layers of carved wooden gilt cloud-dragon patterns on green ground, alternating with eighty-one five-colored cloud backing plates painted.
translations.idiomatic: The heaven-wheel had three red-lacquered layers, fitted above with eighty-one carved wooden gilt-edged radiant leaf plates; inside were three layers of carved gilt cloud dragons on green ground, alternating with eighty-one painted five-colored cloud backing plates.

sentences.zh: 盤下四周，黃銅釘裝，施 黃綺瀝水三層，每層八十一摺，間繡五彩雲龍文。

translations.literal: Below the disk on all four sides were yellow-bronze nail fittings, with three layers of yellow damask drip-water hangings, each layer of eighty-one folds, embroidered between with five-colored cloud-dragon patterns.
translations.idiomatic: Below the disk on all four sides were yellow-bronze nail fittings and three layers of yellow damask drip panels, each with eighty-one folds and embroidered five-colored cloud dragons between.

sentences.zh: 四角垂青綺絡帶，各繡五彩雲 升龍。

translations.literal: At the four corners hung green damask net bands, each embroidered with a five-colored cloud ascending dragon.
translations.idiomatic: At the four corners hung green damask net bands, each embroidered with a five-colored ascending dragon among clouds.

sentences.zh: 圓盤四角連輅坐板，用攀頂黃線圓條，並貼金木魚。

translations.literal: The four corners of the round disk connected to the carriage seat boards, using yellow cord round strips from the climbing top, together with gilt wooden fish.
translations.idiomatic: The four corners of the round disk joined the carriage seat boards, with yellow cord roundels from the finial and gilt wooden fish fittings.

sentences.zh: 輅亭前有左右轉角闌 幹二扇，後一字帶左右轉角闌干一扇，皆紅髹，內嵌雕木貼金龍，間以五彩云。

translations.literal: Before the carriage pavilion were two left and right corner-turning balustrade panels; behind, one single-bar left and right corner-turning balustrade panel—all lacquered red, inset with carved wooden gilt dragons alternating with five-colored clouds.
translations.idiomatic: Before the carriage pavilion were two corner balustrade panels left and right; behind was one single-bar corner balustrade panel—all lacquered red, inset with carved gilt dragons alternating with five-colored clouds.

sentences.zh: 三扇共十二柱，柱首雕木貼金蹲龍及線金五彩蓮花抱柱。

translations.literal: The three panels together had twelve pillars; at the pillar heads were carved wooden gilt crouching dragons and gold-thread five-colored lotus pillar-embracers.
translations.idiomatic: The three panels had twelve pillars altogether, their capitals carved with gilt crouching dragons and gold-thread five-colored lotus pillar wraps.

sentences.zh: 闌干內四周布花毯。

translations.literal: Within the balustrades on all four sides were spread floral carpets.
translations.idiomatic: Inside the balustrades floral carpets were laid on all four sides.

sentences.zh: 亭 後樹太常旗二，以黃線羅爲之，皆十有二斿，每斿內外繡升龍一。

translations.literal: Behind the pavilion were planted two Grand Constant banners, made of yellow cord gauze, each with twelve tassels, each tassel embroidered inside and outside with one ascending dragon.
translations.idiomatic: Behind the pavilion stood two Grand Constant banners of yellow cord gauze, each with twelve tassels embroidered inside and out with an ascending dragon.

sentences.zh: 左旗腰繡日月 北斗，竿首用鍍金銅龍首。

translations.literal: The left banner's waist was embroidered with sun, moon, and the Northern Dipper; the pole head used a gilt-bronze dragon head.
translations.idiomatic: The left banner's midsection was embroidered with the sun, moon, and Northern Dipper; its pole bore a gilt-bronze dragon head.

sentences.zh: 右旗腰繡黻字，竿首用鍍金銅戟。

translations.literal: The right banner's waist was embroidered with the fu character; the pole head used a gilt-bronze halberd.
translations.idiomatic: The right banner's midsection was embroidered with the fu emblem; its pole bore a gilt-bronze halberd head.

sentences.zh: 各綴抹金銅鈴二， 垂紅纓十二，纓上施抹金銅寶蓋，下垂青線帉錔。

translations.literal: On each were attached two gilt-bronze bells; twelve red tassels hung down; above the tassels were set gilt-bronze precious canopies, with green cord streamers hanging below.
translations.idiomatic: Each bore two gilt-bronze bells, twelve red tassels, gilt-bronze precious canopies above the tassels, and green cord streamers below.

sentences.zh: 踏梯一，紅髹，以抹金銅 鈒花葉片裝釘。

translations.literal: One mounting ladder, lacquered red, set with gilt-bronze inlaid floral leaf plates.
translations.idiomatic: There was one mounting ladder, lacquered red and fitted with gilt-bronze inlaid floral leaf plates.

sentences.zh: 行馬架二，紅髹，上有黃絨匾條，用抹金銅葉片裝釘。

translations.literal: Two traveling-horse frames, lacquered red, with yellow plush name plaques above, set with gilt-bronze leaf plates.
translations.idiomatic: There were two traveling-horse frames, lacquered red, each bearing a yellow plush name plaque fitted with gilt-bronze leaf plates.

sentences.zh: 有黃絹幰 衣、

translations.literal: There were yellow silk curtain garments,
translations.idiomatic: There were yellow silk curtain covers,

translations.literal: open bracket

sentences.zh: （即遮塵。）〉

translations.literal: (that is, dust covers.)〉
translations.idiomatic: that is, dust covers.)

sentences.zh: 油絹雨衣、青氈衣及紅油合扇梯、紅油託叉各一。

translations.literal: Oiled-silk rain garments, blue felt garments, and one each of a red-oiled folding fan ladder and red-oiled support fork.
translations.idiomatic: Oiled-silk rain covers, blue felt covers, and one each of a red-oiled folding ladder and red-oiled support fork.

sentences.zh: 輅以二象駕 之。

translations.literal: The carriage was driven by two elephants.
translations.idiomatic: The carriage was drawn by two elephants.

sentences.zh: 玉輅，亦駕以二象，制如大輅，而無平盤下十二槅之飾。

translations.literal: The jade carriage was also driven by two elephants; its form was like the Great Carriage, but without the ornament of the twelve panels below the level platform.
translations.idiomatic: The jade carriage was also drawn by two elephants and followed the Great Carriage in design, but lacked the twelve panels beneath the platform.

sentences.zh: 輅亭前二柱，飾以 搏換貼金升龍。

translations.literal: The front two pillars of the carriage pavilion were ornamented with applique gilt ascending dragons.
translations.idiomatic: The front two pillars of the carriage pavilion were decorated with applique gilt ascending dragons.

sentences.zh: 屏風後無上四槅雲龍及雲板之飾。

translations.literal: Behind the screen there were none of the upper four-panel cloud-dragon and cloud-panel ornaments.
translations.idiomatic: Behind the screen it lacked the upper four cloud-dragon panels and matching cloud panels.

sentences.zh: 天輪內用青地雕木飾玉色雲龍 文。

translations.literal: Within the heaven-wheel carved wood on blue ground was ornamented with jade-colored cloud-dragon patterns.
translations.idiomatic: Inside the heaven-wheel, carved wood on blue ground bore jade-colored cloud dragons.

sentences.zh: 而太常旗及踏梯、行馬之類，悉與大輅同。

translations.literal: But the Grand Constant banners, mounting ladder, traveling horses, and the like were all the same as on the Great Carriage.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Constant banners, mounting ladder, traveling horses, and the like were otherwise the same as on the Great Carriage.

sentences.zh: 大馬輦，古者輦以人挽之。

translations.literal: The large horse sedan: in antiquity sedans were drawn by men.
translations.idiomatic: The large horse sedan: in antiquity such conveyances were pulled by men.

sentences.zh: 《周禮·巾車》後五輅，其一「輦車，組挽」。

translations.literal: In the "Cap-Maker of Carriages" section of the Rites of Zhou, among the rear five carriages, one entry reads "sedan carriage, harness drawing."
translations.idiomatic: The Rites of Zhou, Cap-Maker of Carriages, lists the rear five carriages; one is the "sedan carriage, drawn by harness."

sentences.zh: 然《縣師》有「車輦之稽」，《黍苗》詩云「我任我輦」，則臣民所乘亦名輦。

translations.literal: Yet the "Director of the Districts" has "auditing of carriages and sedans," and the "Millet Sprouts" ode says "I bear, I sedan"—so what subjects and commoners ride is also called a sedan.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the Director of the Districts records "auditing of carriages and sedans," and the "Millet Sprouts" ode says "I bear, I sedan"—so what officials and commoners ride was also called a sedan.

sentences.zh: 至秦始去其輪，而制乃尊。

translations.literal: By the Qin they first removed its wheels, and the institution thereby became exalted.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Qin the wheels were first removed, and the form thereby gained prestige.

sentences.zh: 明諸輦有輪者駕以馬，以別於步輦焉。

translations.literal: In Ming, among sedans those with wheels were driven by horses, to distinguish them from hand sedans.
translations.idiomatic: In Ming, wheeled sedans were horse-drawn to distinguish them from hand sedans.

sentences.zh: 其制，高一丈 二尺五寸九分，廣八尺九寸五分，轅長二丈五寸有奇，輦座高三尺四寸有奇，餘 同大輅。

translations.literal: Its form: twelve feet five and nine-tenths inches in height, eight feet nine and five-tenths inches in width, shafts a little over twenty-five feet long, the sedan seat a little over three feet four inches high—the rest the same as the Great Carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Its dimensions were twelve feet five and nine-tenths inches high, eight feet nine and five-tenths inches wide, with shafts a little over twenty-five feet long and a sedan body a little over three feet four inches high; the rest matched the Great Carriage.

sentences.zh: 輦亭高六尺四寸有奇，紅髹四柱，長五尺四寸有奇。

translations.literal: The sedan pavilion was a little over six feet four inches high, with four pillars lacquered red, a little over five feet four inches long.
translations.idiomatic: The sedan pavilion stood a little over six feet four inches high, with four red-lacquered pillars a little over five feet four inches long.

sentences.zh: 檻座高與輅同，四 周紅髹條環板。

translations.literal: The railing seat was the same height as the carriage; on all four sides were red-lacquered strip ring boards.
translations.idiomatic: The railing base matched the carriage in height, with red-lacquered strip ring boards on all four sides.

sentences.zh: 前左右有門，高五尺有奇，廣二尺四寸有奇。

translations.literal: To the front left and right were doors a little over five feet high and a little over two feet four inches wide.
translations.idiomatic: Doors to the front left and right stood a little over five feet high and a little over two feet four inches wide.

sentences.zh: 門旁槅各二，後槅 三及明栨，皆紅髹，抹金銅鈒花葉片裝釘。

translations.literal: Beside each door were two panels; behind were three panels and open lattices—all lacquered red, set with gilt-bronze inlaid floral leaf plates.
translations.idiomatic: Beside each door were two panels; behind were three panels and open lattices, all lacquered red and fitted with gilt-bronze inlaid floral leaf plates.

sentences.zh: 槅心編以黃線條。

translations.literal: The panel centers were woven with yellow cord strips.
translations.idiomatic: The panel centers were woven with yellow cord.

sentences.zh: 亭內製與大輅同， 第軟座上不用花毯，而用紅毯。

translations.literal: Within the pavilion the form was the same as the Great Carriage, only on the soft seat a floral carpet was not used but a red carpet.
translations.idiomatic: Inside the pavilion it followed the Great Carriage, except the cushioned seat used a red carpet rather than a floral one.

sentences.zh: 亭外用紅簾十二扇。

translations.literal: Outside the pavilion were twelve red curtain panels.
translations.idiomatic: Outside the pavilion hung twelve red curtains.

sentences.zh: 輦頂並圓盤高二尺六寸有奇， 上下俱紅髹，以青飾輦蓋。

translations.literal: The sedan top and round disk together were a little over two feet six inches high; above and below were all lacquered red, with blue ornament on the sedan canopy.
translations.idiomatic: The sedan top and round disk together rose a little over two feet six inches, lacquered red above and below, with blue trim on the canopy.

sentences.zh: 其銅龍、蓮座、寶蓋、黃屋及天輪、輦亭，制悉與大 輅同。

translations.literal: Its bronze dragons, lotus seats, precious canopy, Yellow Canopy, heaven-wheel, and sedan pavilion—all forms were entirely the same as the Great Carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Its bronze dragons, lotus seats, precious canopy, Yellow Canopy, heaven-wheel, and sedan pavilion all matched the Great Carriage.

sentences.zh: 太常旗、踏梯、行馬之屬，亦同大輅。

translations.literal: The Grand Constant banners, mounting ladder, traveling horses, and the like were also the same as on the Great Carriage.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Constant banners, mounting ladder, traveling horses, and the like were the same as on the Great Carriage.

sentences.zh: 駕以八馬，備鞍韉、鞦轡、鈴纓 之飾。

translations.literal: It was driven by eight horses, furnished with saddles, saddle cloths, swing bridles, and bell tassels.
translations.idiomatic: It was drawn by eight horses fitted with saddles, saddle cloths, swing bridles, and bell tassels.

sentences.zh: 小馬輦，視大馬輦高廣皆減一尺，轅長一丈九尺有奇，餘同大馬輦。

translations.literal: The small horse sedan, compared with the large horse sedan, was reduced by one foot in both height and width; the shafts were a little over nineteen feet long—the rest the same as the large horse sedan.
translations.idiomatic: The small horse sedan was one foot shorter in height and width than the large horse sedan, with shafts a little over nineteen feet long; otherwise it matched the large horse sedan.

sentences.zh: 輦亭高 五尺五寸有奇，紅髹四柱，長五尺四寸有奇。

translations.literal: The sedan pavilion was a little over five feet five inches high, with four pillars lacquered red, a little over five feet four inches long.
translations.idiomatic: The sedan pavilion stood a little over five feet five inches high, with four red-lacquered pillars a little over five feet four inches long.

sentences.zh: 檻座紅髹，四周條環板，前左右有 門，高五尺，廣二尺二寸有奇。

translations.literal: The railing seat was lacquered red, with strip ring boards on all four sides; to the front left and right were doors five feet high and a little over two feet two inches wide.
translations.idiomatic: The railing base was red-lacquered with strip ring boards on all sides; doors to the front left and right were five feet high and a little over two feet two inches wide.

sentences.zh: 門旁槅各二及明栨，後屏風壁板，俱紅髹，用 抹金銅鈒花葉片裝釘。

translations.literal: Beside each door were two panels and open lattices; the rear screen wall panels were all lacquered red, set with gilt-bronze inlaid floral leaf plates.
translations.idiomatic: Beside each door were two panels and open lattices; the rear screen panels were red-lacquered and fitted with gilt-bronze inlaid floral leaf plates.

sentences.zh: 亭底紅髹，上施紅花毯、紅錦褥席。

translations.literal: The pavilion floor was lacquered red; above were spread a red floral carpet and red brocade mattress and mat.
translations.idiomatic: The pavilion floor was red-lacquered, covered with a red floral carpet and red brocade bedding.

sentences.zh: 外用紅簾四扇，駕以 四馬。

translations.literal: Outside were four red curtain panels; it was driven by four horses.
translations.idiomatic: Outside hung four red curtains; it was drawn by four horses.

sentences.zh: 餘同大馬輦。

translations.literal: The rest was the same as the large horse sedan.
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise it matched the large horse sedan.

sentences.zh: 步輦者，古之步挽。

translations.literal: The hand sedan was the ancient hand-drawn conveyance.
translations.idiomatic: The hand sedan was the ancient hand-drawn carriage.

sentences.zh: 明制，高一丈三尺二寸有奇，廣八尺二寸有奇。

translations.literal: Under Ming institutions it was a little over thirteen feet two inches high and a little over eight feet two inches wide.
translations.idiomatic: Under Ming regulations it stood a little over thirteen feet two inches high and a little over eight feet two inches wide.

sentences.zh: 輦座高 三尺二寸有奇，四周雕木五彩雲渾貼金龍板十二片，間以渾貼金仰覆蓮座，下雕 木線金五彩雲板十二片。

translations.literal: The sedan seat was a little over three feet two inches high; on all four sides were twelve carved wooden five-colored cloud panels with fully applique gilt dragon boards, alternating with fully applique gilt upturned and downturned lotus seats; below were twelve carved wooden gold-thread five-colored cloud panels.
translations.idiomatic: The sedan body rose a little over three feet two inches, surrounded by twelve carved wooden panels of five-colored clouds with fully applique gilt dragons, alternating with fully applique gilt lotus seats, and twelve carved wooden panels below traced in gold with five-colored clouds.

sentences.zh: 轅四，紅髹。

translations.literal: There were four shafts, lacquered red.
translations.idiomatic: It had four red-lacquered shafts.

sentences.zh: 中二轅長三丈五尺九寸，左右二轅長二丈 九尺五寸有奇，俱以鍍金銅龍頭、龍尾裝釘。

translations.literal: The center two shafts were thirty-five feet nine inches long; the left and right two shafts were a little over twenty-nine feet five inches long—all fitted with gilt-bronze dragon heads and tails.
translations.idiomatic: The center two shafts were thirty-five feet nine inches long; the outer two were a little over twenty-nine feet five inches long—all fitted with gilt-bronze dragon heads and tails.

sentences.zh: 輦亭高六尺三寸有奇，四柱長六尺 二寸有奇。

translations.literal: The sedan pavilion was a little over six feet three inches high; the four pillars were a little over six feet two inches long.
translations.idiomatic: The sedan pavilion stood a little over six feet three inches high, with four pillars a little over six feet two inches long.

sentences.zh: 檻座紅髹，四周雕木沉香色描金香草板十二片，抹金銅鈒花葉片裝釘。

translations.literal: The railing seat was lacquered red; on all four sides were twelve carved wooden panels in agarwood color with gold tracery of herb patterns, set with gilt-bronze inlaid floral leaf plates.
translations.idiomatic: The railing base was red-lacquered, fitted with twelve carved agarwood-colored panels traced in gold with herb motifs and gilt-bronze inlaid floral leaf plates.

sentences.zh: 前左右有門，高五尺七寸有奇，廣二尺四寸有奇。

translations.literal: To the front left and right were doors a little over five feet seven inches high and a little over two feet four inches wide.
translations.idiomatic: Doors to the front left and right stood a little over five feet seven inches high and a little over two feet four inches wide.

sentences.zh: 門旁紅髹十字槅各二扇，雕飾 沉香色描金雲龍板八片，下雲板如其數。

translations.literal: Beside the doors were two red-lacquered cross panels each; eight carved panels in agarwood color with gold-traced cloud-dragons, with cloud panels below in the same number.
translations.idiomatic: Beside each door were two red-lacquered cross panels, eight agarwood-colored panels carved with gold-traced cloud dragons, and matching cloud panels below.

sentences.zh: 後紅髹屏風，上雕沉香色描金雲龍五。

translations.literal: At the rear was a red-lacquered screen, carved above with five agarwood-colored gold-traced cloud-dragons.
translations.idiomatic: At the rear stood a red-lacquered screen carved with five agarwood-colored gold-traced cloud dragons.

sentences.zh: 屏後雕沉香色描金雲龍板三片，又云板如其數，俱用抹金銅鈒花葉片裝釘。

translations.literal: Behind the screen were carved three agarwood-colored gold-traced cloud-dragon panels, and cloud panels again in the same number—all set with gilt-bronze inlaid floral leaf plates.
translations.idiomatic: Behind the screen were three agarwood-colored panels carved with gold-traced cloud dragons and matching cloud panels, all fitted with gilt-bronze inlaid floral leaf plates.

sentences.zh: 餘同 馬輦，惟紅簾用十扇。

translations.literal: The rest was the same as the horse sedan, only ten red curtain panels were used.
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise it matched the horse sedan, except that ten red curtains were used.

sentences.zh: 輦頂並圓盤高二尺六寸有奇，其蓮座、輦蓋、天輪、幰 衣之屬，俱同馬輦。

translations.literal: The sedan top and round disk together were a little over two feet six inches high; the lotus seats, sedan canopy, heaven-wheel, curtain garments, and the like were all the same as on the horse sedan.
translations.idiomatic: The sedan top and round disk together rose a little over two feet six inches; the lotus seats, canopy, heaven-wheel, curtain covers, and the like all matched the horse sedan.

sentences.zh: 大涼步輦，高一丈二尺五寸有奇，廣一丈二尺五寸有奇。

translations.literal: The large cool hand sedan was a little over twelve feet five inches high and a little over twelve feet five inches wide.
translations.idiomatic: The large cool hand sedan stood a little over twelve feet five inches high and a little over twelve feet five inches wide.

sentences.zh: 四面紅髹匡，裝雕 木五彩雲板二十片，間以貼金仰覆蓮座，下紅髹如意條環板，如其數。

translations.literal: On all four sides was a red-lacquered frame, fitted with twenty carved wooden five-colored cloud panels, alternating with applique gilt upturned and downturned lotus seats; below were red-lacquered ruyi strip ring boards in the same number.
translations.idiomatic: On all four sides was a red-lacquered frame fitted with twenty carved five-colored cloud panels, alternating with applique gilt lotus seats and matching red-lacquered ruyi strip ring boards below.

sentences.zh: 紅髹轅六： 中二轅長四丈三尺五寸有奇，左右二轅長四丈有奇，外二轅長三丈六尺五寸有奇， 前後俱飾以雕木貼金龍頭、龍尾。

translations.literal: Six shafts lacquered red: the center two were a little over forty-three feet five inches long; the left and right two were a little over forty feet long; the outer two were a little over thirty-six feet five inches long—front and rear all ornamented with carved wooden applique gilt dragon heads and tails.
translations.idiomatic: It had six red-lacquered shafts: the center pair a little over forty-three feet five inches long, the next pair a little over forty feet, and the outer pair a little over thirty-six feet five inches—all fitted front and rear with carved applique gilt dragon heads and tails.

sentences.zh: 輦亭高六尺五寸有奇，廣八尺五寸有奇，四柱 紅髹。

translations.literal: The sedan pavilion was a little over six feet five inches high and a little over eight feet five inches wide, with four pillars lacquered red.
translations.idiomatic: The sedan pavilion stood a little over six feet five inches high and eight feet five inches wide, with four red-lacquered pillars.

sentences.zh: 前左右有門，高五尺八寸有奇，廣二尺五寸有奇，四周描金香草板十二片。

translations.literal: To the front left and right were doors a little over five feet eight inches high and a little over two feet five inches wide, with twelve gold-traced herb-pattern panels all around.
translations.idiomatic: Doors to the front left and right stood a little over five feet eight inches high and two feet five inches wide, surrounded by twelve panels traced in gold with herb motifs.

sentences.zh: 門旁槅各二，後槅三及明栨皆紅髹，編以黃線條。

translations.literal: Beside each door were two panels; behind were three panels and open lattices, all lacquered red, woven with yellow cord strips.
translations.idiomatic: Beside each door were two panels; behind were three panels and open lattices, all red-lacquered and woven with yellow cord.

sentences.zh: 亭底上施墊氈，加紅錦褥並 席。

translations.literal: On the pavilion floor were spread padding felt, with red brocade mattress and mat added above.
translations.idiomatic: The pavilion floor was padded with felt and covered with red brocade bedding and mats.

sentences.zh: 紅髹坐椅一，四周雕木沉香色，描金寶相花，靠背、褥、裙、帷幔與馬輦同。

translations.literal: One red-lacquered chair; on all four sides carved wood in agarwood color with gold-traced treasure-flower motifs; the backrest, cushions, skirt, and curtains were the same as on the horse sedan.
translations.idiomatic: There was one red-lacquered chair with agarwood-colored carved sides traced in gold with treasure flowers; its backrest, cushions, skirt, and curtains matched the horse sedan.

sentences.zh: 內設紅髹桌二；

translations.literal: Within were set two red-lacquered tables;
translations.idiomatic: Inside were two red-lacquered tables;

sentences.zh: 紅髹闌干香桌一，闌干四，柱首俱雕木貼金蹲龍；

translations.literal: one red-lacquered balustrade incense table, with four balustrades, all pillar heads carved with wooden applique gilt crouching dragons;
translations.idiomatic: one red-lacquered balustrade incense table with four balustrades, their capitals carved with applique gilt crouching dragons;

sentences.zh: 鍍金銅龍蓋香 爐一，並香匙、箸、瓶；

translations.literal: one gilt-bronze dragon-lidded incense burner, together with incense spoon, chopsticks, and vase;
translations.idiomatic: one gilt-bronze incense burner with a dragon lid, together with spoon, chopsticks, and vase;

sentences.zh: 紅錦墩二。

translations.literal: two red brocade cushions.
translations.idiomatic: and two red brocade seat cushions.

sentences.zh: 外紅簾三扇。

translations.literal: Outside were three red curtain panels.
translations.idiomatic: Outside hung three red curtains.

sentences.zh: 輦頂高二尺七寸有奇，又鍍金 銅寶珠頂，帶仰覆蓮座，高一尺三寸有奇；

translations.literal: The sedan top was a little over two feet seven inches high; further there was a gilt-bronze jeweled-pearl finial, with upturned and downturned lotus seats, a little over one foot three inches high;
translations.idiomatic: The sedan top rose a little over two feet seven inches, topped by a gilt-bronze jeweled finial with lotus seats a little over one foot three inches high;

sentences.zh: 垂攀頂黃線圓條四。

translations.literal: four yellow cord round strips hung from the climbing top.
translations.idiomatic: with four yellow cord roundels hanging from the finial.

sentences.zh: 頂用丹漆，上冒 紅氈，四垂以黃氈爲如意雲，黃氈緣條；

translations.literal: The top used cinnabar lacquer; above was covered red felt; on all four sides hung yellow felt as ruyi clouds, with yellow felt border strips;
translations.idiomatic: The top was cinnabar-lacquered and covered with red felt; yellow felt ruyi clouds hung on all four sides with yellow felt borders;

sentences.zh: 四周施黃綺瀝水三層，每層百三十二摺， 間繡五彩雲龍文。

translations.literal: on all four sides were set three layers of yellow damask drip-water hangings, each layer of one hundred thirty-two folds, embroidered between with five-colored cloud-dragon patterns.
translations.idiomatic: and three layers of yellow damask drip panels on all four sides, each with one hundred thirty-two folds and embroidered five-colored cloud dragons between.

sentences.zh: 或用大紅羅冒頂，以黃羅爲如意雲緣條，瀝水亦用黃羅。

translations.literal: Or great red gauze might cover the top, with yellow gauze as ruyi-cloud border strips, and the drip-water also used yellow gauze.
translations.idiomatic: Alternatively the top might be covered in great red gauze, with yellow gauze ruyi-cloud borders and yellow gauze drip panels.

sentences.zh: 頂下 四周以紅氈爲帷，黃氈緣條，四角鍍金銅雲四。

translations.literal: Below the top on all four sides red felt served as curtains, with yellow felt border strips; at the four corners were four gilt-bronze clouds.
translations.idiomatic: Below the top, red felt curtains on all four sides had yellow felt borders, with gilt-bronze clouds at the four corners.

sentences.zh: 亭內寶蓋繡五龍，頂以紅髹木匡， 冒以黃綺爲黃屋，頂心四周繡雲龍各一。

translations.literal: Within the pavilion the precious canopy was embroidered with five dragons; the top used a red-lacquered wooden frame, covered with yellow damask as the Yellow Canopy; at the top center and on all four sides were embroidered one cloud-dragon each.
translations.idiomatic: Inside the pavilion the precious canopy was embroidered with five dragons; a red-lacquered wooden frame was covered in yellow damask as the Yellow Canopy, with one cloud dragon embroidered at the center and on each of the four sides.

sentences.zh: 輦亭四角至輦座，用攀頂黃線圓條四， 並貼金木魚。

translations.literal: From the four corners of the sedan pavilion to the sedan seat were used four yellow cord round strips from the climbing top, together with gilt wooden fish.
translations.idiomatic: From the four corners of the sedan pavilion to the sedan body ran four yellow cord roundels from the finial, with gilt wooden fish fittings.

sentences.zh: 輦亭前左右轉角闌干二扇，後一字帶轉角闌干一扇，皆紅髹，雕木 渾貼金龍，間以五彩雲板。

translations.literal: Before the sedan pavilion were two left and right corner-turning balustrade panels; behind, one single-bar corner-turning balustrade panel—all lacquered red, with carved wood fully applique gilt dragons alternating with five-colored cloud panels.
translations.idiomatic: Before the sedan pavilion were two corner balustrade panels left and right and one single-bar corner panel behind—all red-lacquered, with fully applique gilt carved dragons alternating with five-colored cloud panels.

sentences.zh: 闌干內四周布席。

translations.literal: Within the balustrades on all four sides mats were spread.
translations.idiomatic: Inside the balustrades mats were laid on all four sides.

sentences.zh: 其闌干十二柱之飾及踏梯之屬，俱 與馬輦同。

translations.literal: The ornament of its twelve balustrade pillars and the mounting ladder and the like were all the same as on the horse sedan.
translations.idiomatic: The twelve balustrade pillars, mounting ladder, and the like all matched the horse sedan.

sentences.zh: 轎者，肩行之車。

translations.literal: The palanquin is a vehicle carried on the shoulders.
translations.idiomatic: A palanquin is a shoulder-borne carriage.

sentences.zh: 宋中興以後，皇后嘗乘龍肩輿。

translations.literal: After the restoration of Song, the empress sometimes rode a dragon shoulder carriage.
translations.idiomatic: After the Song restoration, empresses sometimes rode a dragon shoulder palanquin.

sentences.zh: 又以征伐，道路險阻，詔 百官乘轎，名曰：「竹轎子」，亦曰：「竹輿」。

translations.literal: Also because of campaigns, when roads were perilous, an edict ordered all officials to ride palanquins, named the "bamboo palanquin," also called the "bamboo carriage."
translations.idiomatic: During campaigns over difficult terrain, an edict also required officials to ride palanquins called "bamboo palanquins" or "bamboo carriages."

sentences.zh: 元皇帝用象轎，駕以二象。

translations.literal: Yuan emperors used elephant palanquins, driven by two elephants.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan emperors used elephant palanquins drawn by two elephants.

sentences.zh: 至用紅 板轎，則自明始也。

translations.literal: As for using the red board palanquin, this began only with Ming.
translations.idiomatic: The red board palanquin, however, dates only from the Ming.

sentences.zh: 其制，高六尺九寸有奇。

translations.literal: Its form was a little over six feet nine inches high.
translations.idiomatic: It stood a little over six feet nine inches high.

sentences.zh: 頂紅髹。

translations.literal: The top was lacquered red.
translations.idiomatic: The top was red-lacquered.

sentences.zh: 近頂裝圓匡蜊房窗，鍍金 銅火焰寶，帶仰覆蓮座，四角鍍金銅雲朵。

translations.literal: Near the top was fitted a round frame with honeycomb windows, gilt-bronze flame jewels, with upturned and downturned lotus seats, and gilt-bronze clouds at the four corners.
translations.idiomatic: Near the top was a round frame with honeycomb windows, gilt-bronze flame jewels with lotus seats, and gilt-bronze clouds at the four corners.

sentences.zh: 轎槓二，前後以鍍金銅龍頭、龍尾裝 釘，有黃絨墜角索。

translations.literal: Two palanquin poles, front and rear fitted with gilt-bronze dragon heads and tails, with yellow plush corner-drop ropes.
translations.idiomatic: It had two carrying poles fitted front and rear with gilt-bronze dragon heads and tails, with yellow plush corner ropes.

sentences.zh: 四周紅髹板，左右門二，用鍍金銅釘鉸。

translations.literal: On all four sides were red-lacquered boards; to left and right were two doors, using gilt-bronze nail hinges.
translations.idiomatic: The sides were red-lacquered panels with two doors left and right on gilt-bronze hinges.

sentences.zh: 轎內紅髹匡坐椅一， 福壽板一併褥。

translations.literal: Within the palanquin was one red-lacquered frame chair, one fortune-longevity panel together with cushions.
translations.idiomatic: Inside was one red-lacquered chair with a fortune-and-longevity panel and cushions.

sentences.zh: 椅內黃織金綺靠坐褥，四周椅裙，下鋪席並踏褥。

translations.literal: Within the chair were yellow gold-woven damask back and seat cushions, a chair skirt on all four sides; below were spread mat and step cushion.
translations.idiomatic: The chair held yellow gold-woven damask back and seat cushions with a skirt on all four sides, with mat and step cushion below.

sentences.zh: 有黃絹轎衣、 油絹雨衣各一，青氈衣，紅氈緣條雲子。

translations.literal: There were one each of yellow silk palanquin cover and oiled-silk rain cover, a blue felt cover, and red felt border strips with cloud motifs.
translations.idiomatic: There were one yellow silk cover and one oiled-silk rain cover, a blue felt cover, and red felt borders with cloud motifs.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖十三年謁廟，帝及后妃俱乘肩輿出 宮，至奉天門降輿升輅。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Jiajing, when visiting the temple, the emperor and consorts all rode shoulder carriages out of the palace; at the Gate of Receiving Heaven they descended from the carriage and mounted the state carriage.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing 13, when visiting the temple, the emperor and consorts left the palace in shoulder palanquins, then at the Gate of Receiving Heaven dismounted and boarded the state carriage.

sentences.zh: 隆慶四年設郊祀慶成宴，帝乘板輿由歸極門出，入皇極 門，至殿上降輿。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Longqing, when setting the suburban sacrifice completion banquet, the emperor rode a board palanquin out through the Gate of Returning to the Pole, entered through the Gate of Imperial Supremacy, and at the hall ascended and descended from the palanquin.
translations.idiomatic: In Longqing 4, at the suburban sacrifice completion banquet, the emperor rode a board palanquin out through the Gate of Returning to the Pole, entered through the Gate of Imperial Supremacy, and dismounted at the hall.

sentences.zh: 車駕之出，有具服幄殿。

translations.literal: When the imperial procession set out, there was a full-dress canopy hall.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial procession went forth, there was a full-dress canopy pavilion.

sentences.zh: 按《周官》大小次，木架葦障，上下四旁周以幄壩， 以象宮室。

translations.literal: According to the Offices of Zhou, great and small stations used wooden frames and reed screens; above, below, and on all four sides were surrounded with canopy barriers to represent palace chambers.
translations.idiomatic: According to the Offices of Zhou, great and small stations used wooden frames and reed screens, surrounded on all sides with canopy barriers to represent palace chambers.

sentences.zh: 明鹵簿載具服幄殿，儀仗有黃帳房，仍元制也。

translations.literal: The Ming guard of honor records the full-dress canopy hall; among the ceremonial regalia was the yellow tent chamber—still the Yuan institution.
translations.idiomatic: The Ming guard of honor included a full-dress canopy pavilion and a yellow tent chamber among the regalia, still following Yuan practice.

sentences.zh: 帳並帷幕，以黃木棉 布爲之。

translations.literal: The tent and curtains were made of yellow cotton cloth.
translations.idiomatic: Both the tent and its curtains were of yellow cotton cloth.

sentences.zh: 上施獸吻，柱竿紅髹，竿首彩裝蹲獅，氈頂。

translations.literal: Above were set beast finials; the pole shafts were lacquered red; at the pole heads were colorfully fitted crouching lions; the top was felt.
translations.idiomatic: Beast finials crowned the top; the poles were red-lacquered, their heads fitted with painted crouching lions, and the roof was felt.

sentences.zh: 耕根車，世宗朝始造。

translations.literal: The Plough-Root Carriage was first made in the Shizong reign.
translations.idiomatic: The Plough-Root Carriage was first built in the Shizong reign.

sentences.zh: 漢有耕車，晉曰耕根車，俱天子親耕所用。

translations.literal: Han had the ploughing carriage; Jin called it the Plough-Root Carriage—both were what the Son of Heaven used for personal ploughing.
translations.idiomatic: The Han had a ploughing carriage; the Jin called it the Plough-Root Carriage—both were used when the Son of Heaven ploughed in person.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖十年， 帝將耕耤田，詔造耕根車。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Jiajing, when the emperor was about to plough the sacred field, an edict ordered the manufacture of the Plough-Root Carriage.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing 10, as the emperor was about to plough the sacred field, an edict ordered the Plough-Root Carriage built.

sentences.zh: 禮官上言：「考《大明集禮》，耕耤用宋制，乘玉輅， 以耕根車載耒耜同行。

translations.literal: Ritual officials memorialized: "Examining the Collected Rites of the Great Ming, ploughing the sacred field follows Song institutions: ride the jade carriage, and let the Plough-Root Carriage carry the plough and hoe traveling together."
translations.idiomatic: Ritual officials reported: "According to the Collected Rites of the Great Ming, the sacred-field ploughing follows Song practice: the emperor rides the jade carriage while the Plough-Root Carriage carries the plough and hoe alongside."

sentences.zh: 今考儀注，順天府官奉耒耜及穜稑種置彩輿，先於祭 前二日而出。

translations.literal: Now examining the ritual protocols, Shuntian prefectural officials present the plough and hoe and place the early and late grain seeds in a colored carriage, which goes out two days before the sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Under current ritual protocols, Shuntian officials present the plough and hoe and place the early and late grain seeds in a colored carriage sent out two days before the sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 今用耕根車以載耒耜，宜令造車，於祭祀日早進呈，置耒耜，先玉 輅以行。

translations.literal: Now to use the Plough-Root Carriage to carry the plough and hoe, it is fitting to order the carriage made, presented early on the sacrifice day, place the plough and hoe, and go forth before the jade carriage.
translations.idiomatic: The Plough-Root Carriage should now carry the plough and hoe: order the carriage built, present it early on the sacrifice day with the tools aboard, and send it out ahead of the jade carriage.

sentences.zh: 第稽諸禮書，只有圖式，而無高廣尺寸。

translations.literal: Only, examining the ritual books, there are diagram forms but no height and width dimensions.
translations.idiomatic: But the ritual books give only diagrams, with no height or width measurements.

sentences.zh: 宜依今置車式差小，通用青質。

translations.literal: It is fitting to follow the present service-carriage form made somewhat smaller, universally using blue material.
translations.idiomatic: It should follow the present service-carriage form, made somewhat smaller and finished entirely in blue.

sentences.zh: 」 從之。

translations.literal: " This was followed.
translations.idiomatic: " The proposal was approved.

sentences.zh: 皇后輅：一，高一丈一尺三寸有奇，平盤。

translations.literal: The empress's carriage: one, a little over eleven feet three inches high, with a level platform.
translations.idiomatic: The empress's carriage: one, standing a little over eleven feet three inches high, with a level platform.

sentences.zh: 前後車櫺並雁翅，四垂如意滴珠 板。

translations.literal: Front and rear carriage rails together with goose-wing panels, and four hanging ruyi pearl-drop boards.
translations.idiomatic: It had front and rear side rails and goose-wing panels, with four hanging ruyi panels bearing pearl drops.

sentences.zh: 轅長一丈九尺六寸，皆紅髹。

translations.literal: The shafts were nineteen feet six inches long, all lacquered red.
translations.idiomatic: The shafts were nineteen feet six inches long and lacquered red.

sentences.zh: 轅用抹金銅鳳頭、鳳尾、鳳翎葉片裝釘。

translations.literal: The shafts used gilt-bronze phoenix heads, phoenix tails, and phoenix-feather leaf plates as fittings.
translations.idiomatic: The shafts were fitted with gilt-bronze phoenix heads, tails, and feather-shaped leaf plates.

sentences.zh: 平盤 左右垂護泥板及輪二，貫軸一。

translations.literal: From the level platform to left and right hung mud-guard boards and two wheels, with one axle passing through.
translations.idiomatic: From the platform, mud guards hung on either side with two wheels on a single axle.

sentences.zh: 每輪輻十有八，皆紅髹，輞以抹金鈒花銅葉片裝 釘。

translations.literal: Each wheel had eighteen spokes, all lacquered red; the rims were set with gilt inlaid floral copper leaf plates.
translations.idiomatic: Each wheel had eighteen red-lacquered spokes, the rims fitted with gilt inlaid floral copper leaf plates.

sentences.zh: 輪內車轂，用抹金銅鈒蓮花瓣輪盤裝釘，軸中纏黃絨駕轅諸索。

translations.literal: Within the wheel at the hub, gilt-bronze inlaid lotus-petal wheel disks were set as fittings; at the center of the axle yellow plush was wound for the shafts and all driving ropes.
translations.idiomatic: At the hub, gilt-bronze lotus-petal disks were inlaid as fittings, with yellow plush wound around the axle for the shafts and harness ropes.

sentences.zh: 輅亭高五尺 八寸有奇，紅髹四柱。

translations.literal: The carriage pavilion was a little over five feet eight inches high, with four pillars lacquered red.
translations.idiomatic: The carriage pavilion stood a little over five feet eight inches high, with four red-lacquered pillars.

sentences.zh: 檻座上沉香色描金香草板十二片。

translations.literal: On the railing seat were twelve panels in agarwood color with gold tracery of herb patterns.
translations.idiomatic: The railing base bore twelve agarwood-colored panels traced in gold with herb motifs.

sentences.zh: 前左右有門，高四尺五 寸有奇，廣二尺四寸有奇。

translations.literal: To the front left and right were doors a little over four feet five inches high and a little over two feet four inches wide.
translations.idiomatic: Doors to the front left and right stood a little over four feet five inches high and a little over two feet four inches wide.

sentences.zh: 門旁沉香色線金菱花槅各二，下條環板，有明栨， 抹金銅鈒花葉片裝釘。

translations.literal: Beside each door were two panels in agarwood color with gold-thread water-caltrop-flower patterns; below were strip ring panels with open lattices, set with gilt-bronze inlaid floral leaf plates.
translations.idiomatic: Beside each door stood two agarwood-colored panels traced in gold with water-caltrop motifs, with strip ring panels and open lattices below, all fitted with gilt-bronze inlaid floral leaf plates.

sentences.zh: 後紅髹五山屏風，戧金鸞鳳雲文，屏上紅髹板，戧金雲文， 中裝雕木渾貼金鳳一。

translations.literal: At the rear was a red-lacquered five-peak screen, backed with gold phoenix-and-cloud patterns; above the screen were red-lacquered panels backed with gold cloud patterns; at the center was set one carved wood fully applique gilt phoenix.
translations.idiomatic: At the rear stood a red-lacquered five-peak screen with gold-backed phoenix and cloud motifs; red panels above bore gold cloud patterns, and at the center stood one carved phoenix in fully applique gilt.

sentences.zh: 屏後紅髹板，俱用抹金銅鈒花葉片裝釘。

translations.literal: Behind the screen were red-lacquered panels, all set with gilt-bronze inlaid floral leaf plates.
translations.idiomatic: Behind the screen, red-lacquered panels were all fitted with gilt-bronze inlaid floral leaf plates.

sentences.zh: 亭底紅髹，上施 紅花毯、紅錦褥席、紅髹坐椅一。

translations.literal: The pavilion floor was lacquered red; above were spread a red floral carpet, red brocade mat and cushion, and one red-lacquered chair.
translations.idiomatic: The pavilion floor was red-lacquered, furnished with a red floral carpet, red brocade mats, and one red-lacquered chair.

sentences.zh: 靠背雕木線金五彩裝鳳一，上下香草雲板各一， 紅福壽板一併褥。

translations.literal: On the chair back carved wood bore one phoenix in gold-thread five-colored ornament; above and below were one herb-pattern cloud panel each; one red fortune-longevity panel together with cushions.
translations.idiomatic: The chair back bore one carved phoenix traced in gold with five-colored ornament, with herb-pattern cloud panels above and below, a red fortune-and-longevity panel, and cushions.

sentences.zh: 椅中黃織金綺靠坐褥，四周有椅裙，施黃綺帷幔。

translations.literal: Within the chair were yellow gold-woven damask back and seat cushions; on all four sides was a chair skirt; yellow damask curtains were hung.
translations.idiomatic: The chair held yellow gold-woven damask back and seat cushions, a skirt on all four sides, and yellow damask curtains.

translations.literal: open bracket

sentences.zh: （或黃線羅。）〉

translations.literal: (or yellow cord gauze.) close bracket
translations.idiomatic: or yellow cord gauze)

sentences.zh: 外用紅簾十二扇。

translations.literal: Outside were twelve panels of red curtains.
translations.idiomatic: Twelve red curtain panels hung outside.

sentences.zh: 前二柱，戧金，上寶相花，中鸞鳳雲文，下龜文錦。

translations.literal: The front two pillars were backed with gold; above were treasure-flower motifs, in the middle phoenix-and-cloud patterns, and below tortoise-pattern brocade.
translations.idiomatic: The front two pillars had gold backing, with treasure flowers above, phoenix and cloud motifs in the middle, and tortoise-pattern brocade below.

sentences.zh: 輅頂並圓 盤，高二尺有奇，抹金銅立鳳頂，帶仰覆蓮座，垂攀頂黃線圓條四。

translations.literal: The carriage top and round disk together were a little over two feet high, with a gilt-bronze standing-phoenix finial, bearing upturned and downturned lotus seats, and four yellow cord round strips hanging from the climbing top.
translations.idiomatic: The carriage top and round disk together rose a little over two feet, capped by a gilt-bronze standing phoenix with upturned and downturned lotus seats and four yellow cord roundels hanging from the finial.

sentences.zh: 盤上紅髹， 下四周沉香色描金雲文，內青地五彩雲文，以青飾輅蓋。

translations.literal: Above the disk was red lacquer; below on all four sides were agarwood-color gold-traced cloud patterns; within were five-colored cloud patterns on blue ground, with blue used to ornament the carriage canopy.
translations.idiomatic: The disk was red-lacquered above; below on all four sides ran agarwood-colored panels traced in gold with clouds, while inside bore five-colored clouds on blue to trim the carriage canopy.

sentences.zh: 內寶蓋，紅髹匡，鬥以 八頂，冒以黃綺；

translations.literal: Within was a precious canopy with red-lacquered frame, joined in eight peaks, covered with yellow damask;
translations.idiomatic: Inside stood a precious canopy with a red-lacquered frame joined in eight peaks and covered in yellow damask;

sentences.zh: 頂心及四周繡鳳九，並五彩雲文。

translations.literal: at the apex center and on all four sides were embroidered nine phoenixes, together with five-colored cloud patterns.
translations.idiomatic: its apex and four sides were embroidered with nine phoenixes and five-colored cloud motifs.

sentences.zh: 天輪三層，紅髹，上雕木貼 金邊耀葉板七十二片，內飾青地雕木五彩雲鸞鳳文三層，間繪五彩雲襯板七十二 片。

translations.literal: The heaven-wheel had three layers, lacquered red; above were seventy-two carved wooden gilt-edged radiant leaf plates; within were three layers of carved wooden five-colored cloud phoenix-and-cloud patterns on blue ground, alternating with seventy-two painted five-colored cloud backing plates.
translations.idiomatic: The heaven-wheel had three red-lacquered layers, fitted above with seventy-two carved wooden gilt-edged radiant leaf plates; inside were three layers of carved phoenix and cloud motifs in five colors on blue ground, alternating with seventy-two painted cloud backing plates.

sentences.zh: 下四周黃銅裝釘，上施黃綺瀝水三層，間繡鸞鳳文。

translations.literal: Below on all four sides were yellow-bronze nail fittings; above were set three layers of yellow damask drip-water hangings, embroidered between with phoenix patterns.
translations.idiomatic: Below on all four sides were yellow-bronze nail fittings and three layers of yellow damask drip panels embroidered with phoenix motifs.

sentences.zh: 四垂青綺絡帶，繡鸞鳳 各一。

translations.literal: Four hanging green damask net bands, each embroidered with one phoenix.
translations.idiomatic: Four green damask net bands hung down, each embroidered with a phoenix.

sentences.zh: 圓盤四角連輅座板，用攀頂黃線圓條四。

translations.literal: The four corners of the round disk connected to the carriage seat boards, using four yellow cord round strips from the climbing top.
translations.idiomatic: The four corners of the round disk joined the carriage seat boards, with four yellow cord roundels from the finial.

sentences.zh: 輅亭前後有左右轉角闌干各二扇， 內嵌條環板，皆紅髹；

translations.literal: Before and after the carriage pavilion were two left and right corner-turning balustrade panels each; within were inset strip ring panels, all lacquered red;
translations.idiomatic: Before and behind the carriage pavilion were two corner balustrade panels left and right each, with inset strip ring panels, all lacquered red;

sentences.zh: 計十二柱，柱首雕木紅蓮花，線金青綠裝蓮花抱柱。

translations.literal: In all twelve pillars; at the pillar heads carved wood red lotus flowers, with gold-thread blue-green ornament lotus pillar-embracers.
translations.idiomatic: There were twelve pillars in all, their capitals carved as red lotus flowers with gold-thread blue-green lotus pillar-embracers.

sentences.zh: 其踏 梯、行馬之屬，與大馬輦同。

translations.literal: Its mounting ladder, traveling-horse frames, and the like were the same as the large horse sedan.
translations.idiomatic: Its mounting ladder, traveling-horse frames, and the like matched the large horse sedan.

sentences.zh: 安車，本《周禮》後五輅之一。

translations.literal: The Comfort Carriage was originally one of the rear five carriages in the "Rites of Zhou."
translations.idiomatic: The Comfort Carriage was originally one of the rear five carriages in the Rites of Zhou.

sentences.zh: 應劭《漢官鹵簿圖》有五色安車。

translations.literal: Ying Shao's "Illustrated Guard of Honor of Han Offices" records five-colored comfort carriages.
translations.idiomatic: Ying Shao's Illustrated Guard of Honor of Han Offices describes comfort carriages in five colors.

sentences.zh: 晉皇后乘 雲母安車。

translations.literal: The Jin empress rode a mica comfort carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Jin empresses rode in mica-paneled comfort carriages.

sentences.zh: 唐皇后安車，制如金輅。

translations.literal: Tang empress comfort carriages were made like the gold carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Tang empress comfort carriages followed the specifications of the gold carriage.

sentences.zh: 明皇后安車獨簡素。

translations.literal: Ming empress comfort carriages alone were plain and simple.
translations.idiomatic: Ming empress comfort carriages alone were notably plain.

sentences.zh: 其制，高九尺七寸有奇， 平盤，前後車櫺並雁翅板。

translations.literal: Its form was a little over nine feet seven inches high, with a level platform, front and rear carriage rails together with goose-wing panels.
translations.idiomatic: It stood a little over nine feet seven inches high, with a level platform, front and rear side rails, and goose-wing panels.

sentences.zh: 轅二，長一丈六尺七寸有奇，皆紅髹，用抹金銅鳳頭、 鳳尾、鳳翎葉片裝釘。

translations.literal: Two shafts, a little over sixteen feet seven inches long, all lacquered red, using gilt-bronze phoenix heads, phoenix tails, and phoenix-feather leaf plates as fittings.
translations.idiomatic: Two shafts, a little over sixteen feet seven inches long, were lacquered red and fitted with gilt-bronze phoenix heads, tails, and feather-shaped leaf plates.

sentences.zh: 平盤左右垂護泥板及輪二，貫軸一。

translations.literal: To the left and right of the level platform hung mud-guard panels and two wheels, passing through one axle.
translations.idiomatic: Mud guards hung to left and right of the platform, with two wheels on a single axle.

sentences.zh: 每輪輻十有八，皆紅 髹，軸中纏黃絨駕轅諸索。

translations.literal: Each wheel had eighteen spokes, all lacquered red; at the center of the axle yellow plush was wound for the shafts and all driving ropes.
translations.idiomatic: Each wheel had eighteen red-lacquered spokes, with yellow plush wound around the axle for the shafts and harness ropes.

sentences.zh: 車亭高四尺四寸，紅髹方柱四，上裝五彩花板十二片。

translations.literal: The carriage pavilion was four feet four inches high, with four square pillars lacquered red; above were set twelve five-colored floral panels.
translations.idiomatic: The carriage pavilion stood four feet four inches high, with four red-lacquered square pillars and twelve five-colored floral panels above.

sentences.zh: 前左右有門，高三尺七寸有奇，廣二尺二寸有奇。

translations.literal: To the front left and right were doors a little over three feet seven inches high and a little over two feet two inches wide.
translations.idiomatic: Doors to the front left and right stood a little over three feet seven inches high and a little over two feet two inches wide.

sentences.zh: 門旁紅髹十字槅各二。

translations.literal: Beside each door were two red-lacquered cross panels.
translations.idiomatic: Beside each door stood two red-lacquered cross panels.

sentences.zh: 後三山 屏鳳，屏後壁板俱紅髹，用抹金銅鈒花葉片裝釘。

translations.literal: At the rear was a three-peak screen; the wall panels behind the screen were all lacquered red, set with gilt-bronze inlaid floral leaf plates.
translations.idiomatic: At the rear stood a three-peak screen; the wall panels behind were red-lacquered and fitted with gilt-bronze inlaid floral leaf plates.

sentences.zh: 亭底紅髹板，上施紅花毯、紅 錦褥，四周施黃綺帷幔，外用紅簾四扇。

translations.literal: The pavilion floor was a red-lacquered board; above were spread a red floral carpet and red brocade cushions; on all four sides yellow damask curtains were hung; outside were four panels of red curtains.
translations.idiomatic: The pavilion floor was red-lacquered, furnished with a red floral carpet and red brocade cushions, yellow damask curtains on all four sides, and four red curtain panels outside.

sentences.zh: 車蓋用紅髹抹金銅寶珠頂，帶蓮座，高 六寸，四角抹金銅鳳頭，用攀條四，並紅髹木魚。
