translations.literal: The carriage canopy used a red-lacquered gilt-bronze precious-pearl finial, with lotus seat, six inches high; at the four corners were gilt-bronze phoenix heads, using four climbing strips, together with red-lacquered wooden fish.
translations.idiomatic: The carriage canopy bore a red-lacquered gilt-bronze jeweled finial with lotus seat, six inches high; gilt-bronze phoenix heads stood at the four corners, with four climbing strips and red-lacquered wooden fish fittings.

sentences.zh: 蓋施黃綺瀝水三層，銷金鸞鳳 文，鳳頭下垂紅帉錔。

translations.literal: On the canopy were set three layers of yellow damask drip-water hangings with gold-couched phoenix patterns; from the phoenix heads hung red streamers.
translations.idiomatic: The canopy had three layers of yellow damask drip panels with gold-couched phoenix motifs, and red streamers hung from the phoenix heads.

sentences.zh: 其踏梯、行馬、幰衣與輅同。

translations.literal: Its mounting ladder, traveling-horse frames, and curtain garments were the same as on the carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Its mounting ladder, traveling-horse frames, and curtain covers matched the carriage.

sentences.zh: 行障：坐障，自唐、宋有之。

translations.literal: Traveling screens and seated screens have existed since Tang and Song.
translations.idiomatic: Traveling screens and seated screens date back to Tang and Song times.

sentences.zh: 皇后重翟車後，皆有行障六，坐障三，左右夾 車宮人執之。

translations.literal: Behind the empress's heavy pheasant carriage were always six traveling screens and three seated screens, held by palace women flanking the carriage left and right.
translations.idiomatic: Behind the empress's heavy pheasant carriage stood six traveling screens and three seated screens, held by palace women on either side.

sentences.zh: 而《唐書》、《宋史》不載其制。

translations.literal: Yet the "History of Tang" and "History of Song" do not record their specifications.
translations.idiomatic: Neither the History of Tang nor the History of Song records their specifications.

sentences.zh: 《金史》：行障長八尺，高六尺；

translations.literal: The "History of Jin" states: traveling screens were eight feet long and six feet high;
translations.idiomatic: The History of Jin gives traveling screens as eight feet long and six feet high;

sentences.zh: 坐障長七尺，高五尺。

translations.literal: Seated screens measured seven feet in length and five feet in height.
translations.idiomatic: seated screens were seven feet long and five feet high.

sentences.zh: 明皇后用行障、坐障，皆以紅綾爲之，繪升降鸞鳳雲文；

translations.literal: Ming empresses used traveling screens and seated screens, all made of red gauze, painted with ascending and descending phoenix-and-cloud patterns;
translations.idiomatic: Ming empresses used traveling and seated screens of red gauze painted with ascending and descending phoenixes and clouds;

sentences.zh: 行障繪瑞草於瀝水，坐障繪雲文於頂。

translations.literal: On traveling screens auspicious herbs were painted on the drip-water sections; on seated screens cloud patterns were painted at the top.
translations.idiomatic: traveling screens bore auspicious herbs on the drip panels, while seated screens bore cloud motifs at the top.

sentences.zh: 太皇太后、皇太后輅及安車、行障、坐障，制與皇后同。

translations.literal: The carriages, comfort carriages, traveling screens, and seated screens of the Grand Empress Dowager and Empress Dowager were made the same as the empress's.
translations.idiomatic: The carriages, comfort carriages, traveling screens, and seated screens of the grand empress dowager and empress dowager matched the empress's specifications.

sentences.zh: 皇妃車曰鳳轎，與歷代異名。

translations.literal: The imperial consort's carriage was called the phoenix palanquin, a name differing from earlier dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial consort's carriage was called the phoenix palanquin, a name unlike those of earlier dynasties.

sentences.zh: 其制，青頂，上抹金銅珠頂，四角抹金銅飛鳳 各一，垂銀香圓寶蓋並彩結。

translations.literal: Its form had a green top; above was a gilt-bronze pearl finial; at the four corners one gilt-bronze flying phoenix each; silver incense-round precious canopies and colored knots hung down.
translations.idiomatic: It had a green top capped by a gilt-bronze jeweled finial, with a gilt-bronze flying phoenix at each corner, and silver incense-round precious canopies and colored knots hanging below.

sentences.zh: 轎身紅髹木匡，三面篾織紋簟，繪以翟文，抹金銅 鈒花葉片裝釘。

translations.literal: The palanquin body was a red-lacquered wooden frame; on three sides were bamboo-woven patterned mats, painted with pheasant patterns, set with gilt-bronze inlaid floral leaf plates.
translations.idiomatic: The palanquin body was a red-lacquered wooden frame with bamboo-woven patterned mats on three sides painted with pheasant motifs, fitted with gilt-bronze inlaid floral leaf plates.

sentences.zh: 紅髹掆，飾以抹金銅鳳頭、鳳尾。

translations.literal: Red-lacquered carrying poles, ornamented with gilt-bronze phoenix heads and phoenix tails.
translations.idiomatic: Its red-lacquered carrying poles were ornamented with gilt-bronze phoenix heads and tails.

sentences.zh: 青銷金羅緣邊紅簾並看帶， 內紅交牀並坐踏褥。

translations.literal: Green gold-couched gauze bordered red curtains together with viewing ties; within were a red folding couch together with seat and step cushions.
translations.idiomatic: Red curtains with green gold-couched gauze borders and viewing ties enfolded a red folding couch with seat and step cushions within.

sentences.zh: 紅銷金羅轎衣一頂，用銷金寶珠文；

translations.literal: One red gold-couched gauze palanquin cover, using gold-couched precious-pearl patterns;
translations.idiomatic: One red gold-couched gauze palanquin cover bore gold-couched jeweled motifs;

sentences.zh: 瀝水，香草文；

translations.literal: on the drip-water sections, herb patterns;
translations.idiomatic: its drip panels bore herb motifs;

sentences.zh: 看帶並 幃，皆鳳文。

translations.literal: the viewing ties and curtains all bore phoenix patterns.
translations.idiomatic: the viewing ties and curtains were all patterned with phoenixes.

sentences.zh: 紅油絹雨轎衣一。

translations.literal: One red oiled-silk rain palanquin cover.
translations.idiomatic: There was one red oiled-silk rain cover for the palanquin.

sentences.zh: 自皇后以下，皆用行障二，坐障一，第別以彩繪。

translations.literal: From the empress downward, all used two traveling screens and one seated screen, but differed in colored painting.
translations.idiomatic: From the empress downward, all used two traveling screens and one seated screen, differing only in their painted ornament.

sentences.zh: 皇妃行障、坐障，俱紅綾 爲之，繪雲鳳，而行障瀝水繪香草。

translations.literal: Imperial consort traveling screens and seated screens were all made of red gauze, painted with cloud-phoenix patterns; on traveling screens auspicious herbs were painted on the drip-water sections.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial consorts used traveling and seated screens of red gauze painted with cloud phoenixes, with auspicious herbs on the drip panels of the traveling screens.

sentences.zh: 皇太子金輅，高一丈二尺二寸有奇，廣八尺九寸。

translations.literal: The crown prince's gold carriage was a little over twelve feet two inches high and eight feet nine inches wide.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince's gold carriage stood a little over twelve feet two inches high and measured eight feet nine inches wide.

sentences.zh: 轅長一丈九尺五寸。

translations.literal: The shafts were nineteen feet five inches long.
translations.idiomatic: Its shafts measured nineteen feet five inches.

sentences.zh: 輅座 高三尺二寸有奇。

translations.literal: The carriage seat was a little over three feet two inches high.
translations.idiomatic: The carriage body rose a little over three feet two inches.

sentences.zh: 平盤、滴珠板、輪輻、輪輞悉同玉輅。

translations.literal: The level platform, pearl-drop boards, wheel spokes, and wheel rims were all the same as the jade carriage.
translations.idiomatic: The platform, pearl-drop boards, spokes, and rims all matched the jade carriage.

sentences.zh: 輅亭高六尺四寸有奇， 紅髹四柱，長五尺四寸。

translations.literal: The carriage pavilion was a little over six feet four inches high, with four pillars lacquered red, five feet four inches long.
translations.idiomatic: The carriage pavilion stood a little over six feet four inches high, with four red-lacquered pillars five feet four inches long.

sentences.zh: 檻座上四周線金五彩香草板。

translations.literal: On the railing seat on all four sides were gold-thread five-colored herb panels.
translations.idiomatic: The railing base bore gold-thread five-colored herb panels on all four sides.

sentences.zh: 前左右有門，高五尺有奇， 廣二尺四寸有奇。

translations.literal: To the front left and right were doors a little over five feet high and a little over two feet four inches wide.
translations.idiomatic: Doors to the front left and right stood a little over five feet high and a little over two feet four inches wide.

sentences.zh: 門旁槅各二，編紅線條及明栨，皆紅髹。

translations.literal: Beside each door were two panels, woven with red cord strips and open lattices, all lacquered red.
translations.idiomatic: Beside each door stood two panels woven with red cord and open lattices, all lacquered red.

sentences.zh: 後五山屏鳳，青地 上雕木貼金龍五，間以五彩雲文。

translations.literal: At the rear was a five-peak screen; on blue ground were five carved wood applique gilt dragons, alternating with five-colored cloud patterns.
translations.idiomatic: At the rear stood a five-peak screen with five carved gilt dragons on blue ground, alternating with five-colored cloud motifs.

sentences.zh: 屏後紅髹板，皆抹金銅鈒花葉片裝釘。

translations.literal: Behind the screen were red-lacquered panels, all set with gilt-bronze inlaid floral leaf plates.
translations.idiomatic: Behind the screen, red-lacquered panels were all fitted with gilt-bronze inlaid floral leaf plates.

sentences.zh: 紅髹匡 軟座，紅絨墜座，大索四，下垂蓮花墜石，上施紅毯紅錦褥席。

translations.literal: A red-lacquered frame soft seat, red plush pendant seat, four great ropes, lotus-flower pendant stones hanging below; above were spread red carpet and red brocade mat and cushion.
translations.idiomatic: It had a red-lacquered soft seat with red plush pendants, four great ropes with lotus pendant stones hanging below, and red carpet and brocade mats above.

sentences.zh: 紅髹椅一，納板 一併褥。

translations.literal: One red-lacquered chair, one receiving panel together with cushions.
translations.idiomatic: There was one red-lacquered chair with a receiving panel and cushions.

sentences.zh: 椅中紅織金綺靠坐褥，四周有椅裙，施紅羅帷幔，外用青綺緣邊。

translations.literal: Within the chair were red gold-woven damask back and seat cushions; on all four sides was a chair skirt; red gauze curtains were hung; outside green damask bordered the edges.
translations.idiomatic: The chair held red gold-woven damask back and seat cushions with a skirt on all four sides, red gauze curtains within, and green damask edging outside.

sentences.zh: 紅簾 十二扇。

translations.literal: Twelve panels of red curtains.
translations.idiomatic: Twelve red curtain panels hung in place.

sentences.zh: 椅雕貼金龍彩雲，下線金彩雲板一。

translations.literal: On the chair was carved an applique gilt dragon with colored clouds; below was one gold-thread colored-cloud panel.
translations.idiomatic: The chair bore a carved gilt dragon among colored clouds, with one gold-thread cloud panel below.

sentences.zh: 亭內編紅線條。

translations.literal: Within the pavilion were woven red cord strips.
translations.idiomatic: Red cord strips were woven within the pavilion.

sentences.zh: 輅頂並圓盤，高二 尺五寸有奇，又鍍金銅寶珠頂，帶仰覆蓮座，高九寸，垂攀頂紅線圓條四。

translations.literal: The carriage top and round disk together were a little over two feet five inches high; further, a gilt-bronze precious-pearl finial, with upturned and downturned lotus seat, nine inches high, and four red cord round strips hanging from the climbing top.
translations.idiomatic: The carriage top and round disk together rose a little over two feet five inches, capped by a gilt-bronze jeweled finial with upturned and downturned lotus seats nine inches high and four red cord roundels hanging from the finial.

sentences.zh: 盤上 丹漆，下內外皆青地繪雲文，以青飾輅蓋。

translations.literal: Above the disk was cinnabar lacquer; below, inside and outside, were all cloud patterns painted on blue ground, with blue used to ornament the carriage canopy.
translations.idiomatic: The disk was cinnabar-lacquered above; inside and below, blue-ground cloud paintings trimmed the carriage canopy in blue.

sentences.zh: 亭內周圍青斗拱，承以丹漆匡，寶蓋 鬥以八頂，冒以紅綺，頂心繡雲龍，餘繡五彩雲文。

translations.literal: Within the pavilion on all sides were green bracket sets, borne on a cinnabar-lacquered frame; the precious canopy was joined in eight peaks, covered with red damask; at the apex center cloud-dragons were embroidered, the rest embroidered with five-colored cloud patterns.
translations.idiomatic: Green bracket sets lined the pavilion interior, borne on a cinnabar-lacquered frame; the precious canopy joined in eight peaks and covered in red damask, with cloud dragons at the apex and five-colored clouds elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 天輪三層皆紅髹，上雕木貼 金邊耀葉板七十二片，內飾青地雕木貼金雲龍文三層，間繪五彩雲襯板七十二片， 四周黃銅裝釘。

translations.literal: The heaven-wheel's three layers were all lacquered red; above were seventy-two carved wooden gilt-edged radiant leaf plates; within were three layers of carved wooden applique gilt cloud-dragon patterns on blue ground, alternating with seventy-two painted five-colored cloud backing plates; on all four sides were yellow-bronze nail fittings.
translations.idiomatic: The three red-lacquered heaven-wheel layers bore seventy-two carved gilt-edged radiant leaf plates above, three layers of carved gilt cloud dragons on blue within, seventy-two painted cloud backing plates between, and yellow-bronze nail fittings on all four sides.

sentences.zh: 上施紅綺瀝水三層，每層七十二摺，間繡五彩雲龍文。

translations.literal: Above were set three layers of red damask drip-water hangings, each layer of seventy-two folds, embroidered between with five-colored cloud-dragon patterns.
translations.idiomatic: Three layers of red damask drip panels hung above, each with seventy-two folds and embroidered five-colored cloud dragons between.

sentences.zh: 四角之飾 與大輅同，第圓條用紅線。

translations.literal: The corner ornaments were the same as on the Great Carriage, but the round strips used red cord.
translations.idiomatic: The corner ornaments matched the Great Carriage, though the round strips were red cord.

sentences.zh: 輅亭前一字闌干一扇，後一字帶轉角闌干一扇，左右 闌干二扇，內嵌五彩雲板，皆丹漆。

translations.literal: Before the carriage pavilion one single-bar balustrade panel; behind one single-bar corner-turning balustrade panel; left and right two balustrade panels each; within were inset five-colored cloud panels, all cinnabar lacquer.
translations.idiomatic: Before the carriage pavilion stood one single-bar balustrade panel and one single-bar corner panel behind; two balustrade panels left and right, all cinnabar-lacquered with inset five-colored cloud panels.

sentences.zh: 計十四柱，柱首制與大輅同。

translations.literal: In all fourteen pillars; the pillar-head form was the same as on the Great Carriage.
translations.idiomatic: There were fourteen pillars in all, their capitals matching the Great Carriage.

sentences.zh: 亭後建紅旗二， 以紅羅爲之。

translations.literal: Behind the pavilion were erected two red flags, made of red gauze.
translations.idiomatic: Two red gauze flags were erected behind the pavilion.

sentences.zh: 九斿，每斿內外繡升龍一。

translations.literal: Nine streamers; on each streamer inside and outside was embroidered one ascending dragon.
translations.idiomatic: Each of the nine streamers was embroidered inside and out with an ascending dragon.

sentences.zh: 左旗腰繡日月北斗，竿用抹金銅龍首。

translations.literal: On the left flag's waist were embroidered sun, moon, and the Northern Dipper; the pole used a gilt-bronze dragon head.
translations.idiomatic: The left flag's midsection bore embroidered sun, moon, and Northern Dipper motifs on a pole capped with a gilt-bronze dragon head.

sentences.zh: 右旗腰繡黻字，竿用抹金銅戟。

translations.literal: On the right flag's waist was embroidered the fu character; the pole used a gilt-bronze halberd.
translations.idiomatic: The right flag's midsection bore the fu character on a pole topped with a gilt-bronze halberd.

sentences.zh: 綴抹金銅鈴二，垂紅纓。

translations.literal: Two gilt-bronze bells were attached; red tassels hung down.
translations.idiomatic: Two gilt-bronze bells were attached, with red tassels hanging below.

sentences.zh: 其踏梯、行馬之屬，與 玉輅同。

translations.literal: Its mounting ladder, traveling-horse frames, and the like were the same as the jade carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Its mounting ladder, traveling-horse frames, and the like matched the jade carriage.

sentences.zh: 帳房用青木棉布，竿首青綠蹲猊，餘同乘輿帳房。

translations.literal: The tent chamber used blue cotton cloth on wooden frames; at the pole top a blue-green crouching lion; the rest was the same as the imperial carriage tent chamber.
translations.idiomatic: The tent chamber used blue cotton on wooden frames, with a blue-green crouching lion at the pole top; otherwise it matched the imperial carriage tent chamber.

sentences.zh: 東宮妃車，亦曰鳳轎、小轎，制同皇妃。

translations.literal: The Eastern Palace consort's carriage, also called the phoenix palanquin or small palanquin, was made the same as the imperial consort's.
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern Palace consort's carriage, also called the phoenix or small palanquin, followed the imperial consort's specifications.

sentences.zh: 行障、坐障之制亦同。

translations.literal: The specifications for traveling screens and seated screens were also the same.
translations.idiomatic: Its traveling and seated screens followed the same specifications.

sentences.zh: 親王象輅，其高視金輅減六寸，其廣減一尺。

translations.literal: The imperial prince's ivory carriage: its height compared with the gold carriage was reduced by six inches; its width reduced by one foot.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial prince's ivory carriage stood six inches lower and one foot narrower than the crown prince's gold carriage.

sentences.zh: 轅長視大輅減一尺。

translations.literal: The shaft length compared with the Great Carriage was reduced by one foot.
translations.idiomatic: Its shafts were one foot shorter than those of the Great Carriage.

sentences.zh: 輅座高三 尺有奇，餘飾同金輅。

translations.literal: The carriage seat was a little over three feet high; the remaining ornament was the same as the gold carriage.
translations.idiomatic: The carriage body rose a little over three feet; otherwise its ornament matched the gold carriage.

sentences.zh: 輅亭高五尺二寸有奇，紅髹四柱。

translations.literal: The carriage pavilion was a little over five feet two inches high, with four pillars lacquered red.
translations.idiomatic: The carriage pavilion stood a little over five feet two inches high, with four red-lacquered pillars.

sentences.zh: 檻座上四周紅髹條環板。

translations.literal: On the railing seat on all four sides were red-lacquered strip ring panels.
translations.idiomatic: The railing base bore red-lacquered strip ring panels on all four sides.

sentences.zh: 前左右有門，高四尺五寸有奇，廣二尺二寸有奇。

translations.literal: To the front left and right were doors a little over four feet five inches high and a little over two feet two inches wide.
translations.idiomatic: Doors to the front left and right stood a little over four feet five inches high and a little over two feet two inches wide.

sentences.zh: 門旁槅各二及明栨、後五山 屏風，皆紅髹，用抹金銅鈒花葉片裝釘。

translations.literal: Beside each door were two panels and open lattices; at the rear a five-peak screen—all lacquered red, set with gilt-bronze inlaid floral leaf plates.
translations.idiomatic: Beside each door stood two panels and open lattices; the rear five-peak screen was red-lacquered and fitted with gilt-bronze inlaid floral leaf plates.

sentences.zh: 亭底紅髹，施紅花毯、紅錦褥席。

translations.literal: The pavilion floor was lacquered red; a red floral carpet and red brocade mat and cushion were spread.
translations.idiomatic: The pavilion floor was red-lacquered, furnished with a red floral carpet and red brocade mats.

sentences.zh: 其椅 靠、坐褥、帷幔、紅簾之制，俱同金輅。

translations.literal: Its chair back, seat cushions, curtains, and red curtain specifications were all the same as the gold carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Its chair back, seat cushions, curtains, and red curtains all matched the gold carriage.

sentences.zh: 輅頂並圓盤，高二尺四寸有奇，用抹金 銅寶珠頂，餘同金輅。

translations.literal: The carriage top and round disk together were a little over two feet four inches high, using a gilt-bronze precious-pearl finial; the rest was the same as the gold carriage.
translations.idiomatic: The carriage top and round disk together rose a little over two feet four inches, with a gilt-bronze jeweled finial; the rest matched the gold carriage.

sentences.zh: 天輪三層，皆紅髹，上雕木貼金邊耀葉板六十三片，內飾 青地雕木五彩雲文三層，間繪五彩雲襯板六十三片，四周黃銅裝釘。

translations.literal: The heaven-wheel had three layers, all lacquered red; above were sixty-three carved wooden gilt-edged radiant leaf plates; within were three layers of carved wooden five-colored cloud patterns on blue ground, alternating with sixty-three painted five-colored cloud backing plates; on all four sides were yellow-bronze nail fittings.
translations.idiomatic: The three red-lacquered heaven-wheel layers bore sixty-three carved gilt-edged radiant leaf plates above, three layers of carved five-colored clouds on blue within, sixty-three painted cloud backing plates between, and yellow-bronze nail fittings on all four sides.

sentences.zh: 上施紅綺瀝 水三層，每層八十一摺，繡瑞草文。

translations.literal: Above were set three layers of red damask drip-water hangings, each layer of eighty-one folds, embroidered with auspicious herb patterns.
translations.idiomatic: Three layers of red damask drip panels hung above, each with eighty-one folds and embroidered with auspicious herb motifs.

sentences.zh: 前垂青綺絡帶二，俱繡升龍五彩雲文。

translations.literal: In front hung two green damask net bands, both embroidered with ascending-dragon five-colored cloud patterns.
translations.idiomatic: Two green damask net bands hung at the front, both embroidered with ascending dragons among five-colored clouds.

sentences.zh: 圓盤 四角連輅座板，用攀頂紅線圓條四，並紅髹木魚。

translations.literal: The four corners of the round disk connected to the carriage seat boards, using four red cord round strips from the climbing top, together with red-lacquered wooden fish.
translations.idiomatic: The four corners of the round disk joined the carriage seat boards, with four red cord roundels from the finial and red-lacquered wooden fish fittings.

sentences.zh: 亭前後闌干同金輅，左右闌干 各一扇，內嵌條環板，皆紅髹。

translations.literal: The pavilion's front and rear balustrades were the same as the gold carriage; left and right balustrades one panel each; within were inset strip ring panels, all lacquered red.
translations.idiomatic: The pavilion's front and rear balustrades matched the gold carriage; one balustrade panel stood to each side, all red-lacquered with inset strip ring panels.

sentences.zh: 計十四柱，柱首雕木紅蓮花，線金青綠裝蓮花抱 柱，前闌干內布花毯。

translations.literal: In all fourteen pillars; the pillar heads were carved wooden red lotuses; gold-thread blue-green enamel lotus embrace-pillars; within the front balustrade a floral carpet was spread.
translations.idiomatic: There were fourteen pillars capped with carved red lotuses, with gold-thread blue-green lotus embrace-pillars; a floral carpet was spread within the front balustrade.

sentences.zh: 紅旗二，與金輅所樹同，竿上只垂紅纓五。

translations.literal: Two red flags, the same as those erected on the gold carriage; on the pole only five red tassels hung down.
translations.idiomatic: Two red flags matched those raised on the gold carriage, with only five red tassels hanging from each pole.

sentences.zh: 其踏梯、行馬 之屬，亦同金輅。

translations.literal: Its mounting ladder, traveling-horse frames, and the like were also the same as the gold carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Its mounting ladder, traveling-horse frames, and the like also matched the gold carriage.

sentences.zh: 帳房用綠色螭頭，餘與東宮同。

translations.literal: The tent chamber used green chih-dragon heads; the rest was the same as the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: The tent chamber bore green chih-dragon finials; otherwise it matched the Eastern Palace specifications.

sentences.zh: 親王妃車，亦曰鳳轎、小轎，制俱同東宮妃。

translations.literal: The imperial prince's consort's carriage, also called the phoenix palanquin or small palanquin, specifications all the same as the Eastern Palace consort.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial prince's consort's carriage, also called the phoenix or small palanquin, followed the Eastern Palace consort's specifications entirely.

sentences.zh: 惟鳳轎衣用木紅平羅。

translations.literal: Only the phoenix palanquin cover used tree-red plain gauze.
translations.idiomatic: Only the phoenix palanquin cover was made of tree-red plain gauze.

sentences.zh: 小轎衣 二：一用礬紅素紵絲，一用木紅平羅。

translations.literal: Small palanquin covers two: one used alum-red plain pongee silk, one used tree-red plain gauze.
translations.idiomatic: There were two small palanquin covers: one of plain alum-red pongee silk and one of tree-red plain gauze.

sentences.zh: 行障、坐障，制同東宮妃。

translations.literal: Traveling screens and seated screens: specifications the same as the Eastern Palace consort.
translations.idiomatic: Its traveling and seated screens matched the Eastern Palace consort's specifications.

sentences.zh: 公主車，宋用厭翟車，明初因之。

translations.literal: Princess carriages: under Song they used the yan-di carriage; early Ming followed this.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial princesses' carriages: the Song used the yan-di carriage, and early Ming followed suit.

sentences.zh: 其後定制，鳳轎、行障、坐障，如親王妃。

translations.literal: Thereafter fixed regulations: phoenix palanquin, traveling screens, seated screens, like the imperial prince's consort.
translations.idiomatic: Later regulations specified phoenix palanquins, traveling screens, and seated screens like those of an imperial prince's consort.

sentences.zh: 皇孫車，永樂中，定皇太孫婚禮儀仗如親王，降皇太子一等，而用象輅。

translations.literal: Imperial grandson carriages: in the Yongle reign, it was fixed that the heir apparent's son's wedding ceremonial guard was like an imperial prince, one rank below the crown prince, using the ivory carriage.
translations.idiomatic: During Yongle, the imperial heir's son was granted wedding ceremonial guard like a prince, one rank below the crown prince, with an ivory carriage.

sentences.zh: 郡王無輅，只有帳房，制同親王。

translations.literal: Commandery princes had no carriage; they only had tent chambers, specifications the same as imperial princes.
translations.idiomatic: Commandery princes were granted no state carriage, only tent chambers matching those of imperial princes.

sentences.zh: 郡王妃及郡主俱用翟轎，制與皇妃鳳轎同，第易鳳爲翟。

translations.literal: Commandery prince's consorts and commandery ladies all used the di palanquin; specifications the same as the imperial consort's phoenix palanquin, but changing phoenix to di.
translations.idiomatic: Commandery princesses and their daughters used di palanquins built like imperial consorts' phoenix palanquins, but with pheasants in place of phoenixes.

sentences.zh: 行障、坐障同親王 妃，而繪雲翟文。

translations.literal: Traveling screens and seated screens the same as the imperial prince's consort, but painted with cloud-di patterns.
translations.idiomatic: Their traveling and seated screens matched an imperial prince's consort's, but were painted with cloud and pheasant motifs.

sentences.zh: 百官乘車之制：洪武元年令，凡車不得雕飾龍鳳文。

translations.literal: Regulations for all officials' carriages: the first year of Hongwu order, all carriages were not permitted carved dragon-phoenix ornament.
translations.idiomatic: Regulations for officials' carriages: a Hongwu first-year order forbade dragon or phoenix ornament on any carriage.

sentences.zh: 職官一品至三品，用間 金飾銀螭繡帶，青縵。

translations.literal: Officials of ranks one through three used spaced gold-decorated silver chih-dragon embroidered bands and blue awnings.
translations.idiomatic: Ranks one through three used awnings with gold-spaced silver chih-dragon embroidered bands and blue covers.

sentences.zh: 四品五品，素獅頭繡帶，青縵。

translations.literal: Ranks four and five, plain lion-head embroidered bands, blue awnings.
translations.idiomatic: Ranks four and five used plain lion-head embroidered bands and blue awnings.

sentences.zh: 六品至九品，用素雲頭青 帶，青縵。

translations.literal: Ranks six through nine used plain cloud-head blue bands, blue awnings.
translations.idiomatic: Ranks six through nine used plain cloud-head blue bands and blue awnings.

sentences.zh: 轎同車制。

translations.literal: Palanquins followed the carriage regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Palanquins followed the same regulations as carriages.

sentences.zh: 庶民車及轎，並用黑油，齊頭平頂，皁縵，禁用雲頭。

translations.literal: Commoners' carriages and palanquins all used black oil, flush-head flat-top, black awnings; cloud-heads were forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: Commoners' carriages and palanquins were black-lacquered with flat tops and black awnings; cloud-head ornament was forbidden.

sentences.zh: 六 年令，凡車轎禁丹漆，五品以上車止用青縵。

translations.literal: Sixth-year order: all carriages and palanquins forbade cinnabar lacquer; carriages of rank five and above used only blue awnings.
translations.idiomatic: A sixth-year order banned cinnabar lacquer on all carriages and palanquins; carriages of the fifth rank and above were limited to blue awnings.

sentences.zh: 婦女許坐轎，官民老疾者亦得乘之。

translations.literal: Women were permitted to ride palanquins; officials and commoners who were old or infirm also obtained permission to ride them.
translations.idiomatic: Women were allowed palanquins, and aged or infirm officials and commoners could ride them as well.

sentences.zh: 景泰四年令，在京三品以上得乘轎。

translations.literal: Fourth year of Jingtai order: in the capital, rank three and above obtained permission to ride palanquins.
translations.idiomatic: A Jingtai fourth-year order allowed officials of the third rank and above in the capital to ride palanquins.

sentences.zh: 弘治七年令，文武官例應乘轎者，以四人舁 之。

translations.literal: Seventh year of Hongzhi order: civil and military officials for whom palanquin riding was standard were borne by four men.
translations.idiomatic: A Hongzhi seventh-year order required civil and military officials entitled to palanquins to be carried by four bearers.

sentences.zh: 其五府管事，內外鎮守、守備及公、侯、伯、都督等，不問老少，皆不得乘 轎，違例乘轎及擅用八人者，奏聞。

translations.literal: The Five Chief Offices stewards, inner and outer garrison commanders, defense commanders, dukes, marquises, earls, regional commanders, and the like, regardless of age, all were not permitted to ride palanquins; those who violated regulations by riding palanquins or presumptuously using eight bearers were reported to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Stewards of the Five Chief Offices, garrison and defense commanders, dukes, marquises, earls, and regional commanders were barred from palanquins regardless of age; violations and unauthorized use of eight bearers were reported to the throne.

sentences.zh: 蓋自太祖不欲勳臣廢騎射，雖上公，出必乘 馬。

translations.literal: This was because from the founding emperor's time he did not wish meritorious ministers to abandon mounted archery; even highest nobles, going out inevitably rode horses.
translations.idiomatic: The founding emperor had wished to keep meritorious officials skilled in mounted archery; even the highest nobles were expected to ride when abroad.

sentences.zh: 永樂元年，駙馬都尉胡觀越制乘晉王濟熹朱<車尞>棕轎，爲給事中周景所劾。

translations.literal: First year of Yongle, imperial son-in-law Commandant Hu Guan exceeded regulations by riding Prince Ji Xi of Jin's red open bracket carriage unit close bracket brown palanquin, and was impeached by Supervising Secretary Zhou Jing.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongle's first year, Imperial Son-in-law Commandant Hu Guan exceeded his rank by riding Prince Ji Xi of Jin's red-framed brown palanquin and was impeached by Supervising Secretary Zhou Jing.

sentences.zh: 有詔宥觀而賜濟熹書，切責之。

translations.literal: There was an edict pardoning Guan and bestowing Ji Xi a letter, sternly reprimanding him.
translations.idiomatic: An edict pardoned Guan but sent Ji Xi a letter of sharp rebuke.

sentences.zh: 惟文職大臣乘轎，庶官亦乘馬。

translations.literal: Only civil chief ministers rode palanquins; common officials also rode horses.
translations.idiomatic: Only senior civil officials rode palanquins; lesser officials rode horses as well.

sentences.zh: 又文臣皆許乘 車，大臣得乘安車。

translations.literal: Moreover all civil ministers were permitted to ride carriages; chief ministers obtained permission to ride the secure carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Civil officials were also permitted carriages, and senior ministers might ride the secure carriage.

sentences.zh: 後久廢不用。

translations.literal: Later this was long abandoned and unused.
translations.idiomatic: This practice was later abandoned for a long time.

sentences.zh: 正德四年，禮部侍郎劉機言，《大明集禮》， 公卿大臣得乘安車，因請定轎扇傘蓋品級等差。

translations.literal: Fourth year of Zhengde, Vice Minister of Rites Liu Ji spoke: the Collected Rites of Great Ming states that dukes and ministers obtain permission to ride the secure carriage; he therefore requested fixing palanquin, fan, parasol, and canopy rank gradations.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengde's fourth year, Vice Minister of Rites Liu Ji cited the Collected Rites of Great Ming, which granted secure carriages to dukes and ministers, and asked that rank gradations for palanquins, fans, parasols, and canopies be fixed.

sentences.zh: 帝以京城內安車傘蓋久不行，卻 其請，而命轎扇俱如例行。

translations.literal: The emperor, on the grounds that within the capital secure carriages, parasols, and canopies had long gone unpracticed, rejected his request, and ordered palanquins and fans all to follow routine practice.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rejected the request because secure carriages, parasols, and canopies had long fallen out of use in the capital, and ordered palanquins and fans to follow ordinary practice.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖十五年，禮部尚書霍韜言：「禮儀定式，京官三 品以上乘轎，邇者文官皆用肩輿，或乘女轎。

translations.literal: Fifteenth year of Jiajing, Minister of Rites Huo Tao spoke: "In the Prescribed Rites, capital officials of rank three and above ride palanquins; recently civil officials all use shoulder litters, or ride women's palanquins.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing's fifteenth year, Minister of Rites Huo Tao said: "The Prescribed Rites allow capital officials of the third rank and above palanquins, yet lately civil officials all use shoulder litters or women's palanquins.

sentences.zh: 乞申明禮制，俾臣下有所遵守。

translations.literal: I beg to clarify the ritual regulations, so that ministers below may have something to observe.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that the ritual regulations be clearly restated so officials may know what to follow.

sentences.zh: 」 乃定四品下不許乘轎，亦毋得用肩輿。

translations.literal: " Thereupon it was fixed that below rank four palanquins were not permitted, and shoulder litters also were not to be used.
translations.idiomatic: The court then barred officials below the fourth rank from palanquins and from shoulder litters as well.

sentences.zh: 隆慶二年，給事中徐尚劾應城伯孫文棟等 乘轎出入，驕僣無狀。

translations.literal: Second year of Longqing, Supervising Secretary Xu Shang impeached Yingcheng Earl Sun Wendong and others for riding palanquins in and out, arrogant and presumptuous beyond measure.
translations.idiomatic: In Longqing's second year, Supervising Secretary Xu Shang impeached Yingcheng Earl Sun Wendong and others for riding palanquins in public with outrageous presumption.

sentences.zh: 帝命奪文棟等俸。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Wendong's and the others' salaries seized.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Wendong and the others stripped of salary.

sentences.zh: 乃諭兩京武職非奉特恩不許乘轎，文官 四品以下用帷轎者，禁如例。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict was issued to both capitals that military offices, unless granted special favor, were not permitted to ride palanquins; civil officials below rank four using curtained palanquins were forbidden as per precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Edicts to both capitals then barred military officers from palanquins unless specially favored, and forbade civil officials below the fourth rank curtained palanquins as before.

sentences.zh: 萬曆三年奏定勳戚及武臣不許用帷轎、肩輿並交牀 上馬。

translations.literal: Third year of Wanli memorial fixed that meritorious kin and military ministers were not permitted to use curtained palanquins, shoulder litters, and mounting-stool horse mounting.
translations.idiomatic: In Wanli's third year it was decreed that meritorious kin and military officers might not use curtained palanquins, shoulder litters, or mounting stools to mount their horses.

sentences.zh: 至若破格殊典，則宣德中少保黃淮陪遊西苑，嘗乘肩輿入禁中。

translations.literal: As for violations of rank and special precedents: in Xuande's reign Junior Guardian Huang Huai accompanied tours of the Western Park and once rode a shoulder litter into the forbidden precinct.
translations.idiomatic: Extraordinary exceptions did occur: during Xuande Junior Guardian Huang Huai once rode a shoulder litter into the forbidden precinct while touring the Western Park.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖間， 嚴嵩奉詔苑直，年及八旬，出入得乘肩輿。

translations.literal: During Jiajing, Yan Song received an edict to serve at the park, his years reaching eighty; going in and out he obtained permission to ride a shoulder litter.
translations.idiomatic: During Jiajing, Yan Song, ordered to serve at the imperial park at age eighty, was permitted a shoulder litter when coming and going.

sentences.zh: 武臣則郭勳、朱希忠特命乘肩輿扈南 巡蹕，後遂賜常乘焉。

translations.literal: Among military ministers Guo Xun and Zhu Xizhong were specially ordered to ride shoulder litters escorting the southern tour retinue; afterward they were granted regular use.
translations.idiomatic: Military officers Guo Xun and Zhu Xizhong were specially permitted shoulder litters on the southern tour, and later granted them for regular use.

sentences.zh: 皆非制也。

translations.literal: All were not according to regulation.
translations.idiomatic: None of these conformed to regulation.

sentences.zh: 傘蓋之制：洪武元年，令庶民不得用羅絹涼傘，但許用油紙雨傘。

translations.literal: Regulations for parasols and canopies: first year of Hongwu, ordered that commoners were not permitted to use gauze-silk cool parasols; only oiled-paper rain umbrellas were allowed.
translations.idiomatic: Parasol and canopy regulations: a Hongwu first-year order barred commoners from silk cool parasols and allowed only oiled-paper rain umbrellas.

sentences.zh: 三年，令 京城內一品二品用傘蓋，其餘用雨傘。

translations.literal: Third year, ordered that within the capital ranks one and two used parasol-canopies; the rest used rain umbrellas.
translations.idiomatic: A third-year order allowed only ranks one and two parasol-canopies within the capital; all others used rain umbrellas.

sentences.zh: 十六年，令尚書、侍郎、左右都御史、通 政使、太常卿、應天府尹、國子祭酒、翰林學士許張傘蓋。

translations.literal: Sixteenth year, ordered that ministers, vice ministers, left and right censors-in-chief, transmission commissioners, grand court ceremonialists, Yingtian prefect, imperial academy chancellor, and Hanlin academicians were permitted to deploy parasols and canopies.
translations.idiomatic: A sixteenth-year order permitted ministers, vice ministers, censors-in-chief, transmission commissioners, grand court ceremonialists, the Yingtian prefect, the imperial academy chancellor, and Hanlin academicians to use parasols and canopies.

sentences.zh: 二十六年定一品、二 品傘用銀浮屠頂，三品、四品用紅浮屠頂，俱用黑色茶褐羅表，紅絹裹，三檐；

translations.literal: Twenty-sixth year fixed: ranks one and two parasols used silver pagoda finials; ranks three and four used red pagoda finials; all used black tea-brown gauze exterior, red silk lining, three tiers;
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year ranks one and two were assigned silver pagoda-finial parasols and ranks three and four red pagoda-finial parasols, all with black tea-brown gauze exteriors, red silk linings, and three tiers;

sentences.zh: 雨傘用紅油絹。

translations.literal: Rain umbrellas used red oiled silk.
translations.idiomatic: Their rain umbrellas were of red oiled silk.

sentences.zh: 五品紅浮屠頂，青羅表，紅絹裹，兩檐；

translations.literal: Rank five: red pagoda finial, blue gauze exterior, red silk lining, two tiers;
translations.idiomatic: Rank five used red pagoda-finial parasols with blue gauze exteriors, red silk linings, and two tiers;

sentences.zh: 雨傘同。

translations.literal: Rain umbrellas the same.
translations.idiomatic: Rain umbrellas followed the same rule.

sentences.zh: 四品、六品至 九品，用紅浮屠頂，青絹表，紅絹裹，兩檐；

translations.literal: Ranks four and six through nine used red pagoda finials, blue silk exterior, red silk lining, two tiers;
translations.idiomatic: Ranks four and six through nine used red pagoda-finial parasols with blue silk exteriors, red silk linings, and two tiers;

sentences.zh: 雨傘俱用油紙。

translations.literal: Rain umbrellas all used oiled paper.
translations.idiomatic: Their rain umbrellas were all oiled paper.

sentences.zh: 三十五年，官員傘 蓋不許用金繡，朱丹裝飾。

translations.literal: Thirty-fifth year, officials' parasols and canopies were not permitted gold embroidery or cinnabar-red decoration.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-fifth year officials were forbidden gold embroidery or cinnabar ornament on parasols and canopies.

sentences.zh: 公、侯、駙馬、伯與一品、二品同。

translations.literal: Dukes, marquises, imperial sons-in-law, and earls were the same as ranks one and two.
translations.idiomatic: Dukes, marquises, imperial sons-in-law, and earls followed the rank-one and rank-two specifications.

sentences.zh: 成化九年，令兩 京官遇雨任用油傘，其涼傘不許張於京城。

translations.literal: Ninth year of Chenghua, ordered that officials of both capitals when encountering rain could use oiled umbrellas at discretion; cool parasols were not permitted opened within the capital.
translations.idiomatic: A Chenghua ninth-year order allowed officials in both capitals to use oiled umbrellas in rain, but forbade opening cool parasols within the capital.

sentences.zh: 鞍轡之制：洪武六年，令庶民不得描金，惟銅鐵裝飾。

translations.literal: Regulations for saddles and bridles: sixth year of Hongwu, ordered that commoners were not permitted gold tracery, only copper and iron ornament.
translations.idiomatic: Saddle and bridle regulations: a Hongwu sixth-year order barred commoners from gold tracery and allowed only copper and iron ornament.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，定公、侯、 一品、二品用銀，鐵事件，<革佔>用描銀。

translations.literal: Twenty-sixth year fixed: dukes, marquises, ranks one and two used silver, iron fittings; open bracket ge zhan close bracket used silver tracery.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year dukes, marquises, and ranks one and two were assigned silver fittings and leather flaps with silver tracery.

sentences.zh: 三品至五品，用銀，鐵事件， <革佔>用油畫。

translations.literal: Ranks three through five used silver, iron fittings; open bracket ge zhan close bracket used oil painting.
translations.idiomatic: Ranks three through five used silver fittings and oil-painted leather flaps.

sentences.zh: 六品至九品，用擺錫，鐵事件，<革佔>用油畫。

translations.literal: Ranks six through nine used pewter plating, iron fittings; open bracket ge zhan close bracket used oil painting.
translations.idiomatic: Ranks six through nine used pewter plating, iron fittings, and oil-painted leather flaps.

sentences.zh: 三十五年，官民人等 馬頷下纓並鞦轡俱用黑色，不許紅纓及描金、嵌金、天青、硃紅裝飾。

translations.literal: Thirty-fifth year, officials and commoners alike: horses' chin tassels and crupper bridles all used black; red tassels and gold tracery, inlaid gold, sky-blue, and cinnabar-red ornament were not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-fifth year chin tassels and crupper bridles for all were restricted to black, barring red tassels and gold tracery, inlaid gold, sky-blue, or cinnabar ornament.

sentences.zh: 軍民用 鐵事件，黑綠油<革佔>。

translations.literal: Military and commoners used iron fittings, black-green oiled open bracket ge zhan close bracket.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers and commoners used iron fittings and black-green oiled leather flaps.
